#3402. Casting Director Francine Maisler on ‘Dune: Part Three’

When Denis Villeneuve brought on seasoned casting director Francine Maisler for the first Dune movie, they were starting from scratch. For the ambitious adaptation of Frank Herbert’s 1965 sci-fi novel, they had to cast not only the lead character, Paul Atreides, but dozens of other main characters—powerful warriors, scheming royals, shape-shifting conspirators—to inhabit the world.

Luckily, the pair had already worked together on Villeneuve’s three previous films, Sicario, Blade Runner 2049, and Arrival. “Denis’s vision is my compass,” Maisler tells Vanity Fair. “His passion [for Dune] since he was a teen was all I needed to follow.”

When they were casting the first installment, Maisler was aware that it was possible that these actors might play these characters for more than just one film. “I did have an idea that they would have to have the presence and the acting talent to be able to carry this potentially for three movies,” she says.

Dune (2021), starring Timothée Chalamet as Paul Atreides and Zendaya as Chani, was just the first step. Maisler returned to cast Dune: Part Two (2024), and Dune: Part Three, which will wrap up Villeneuve’s trilogy when it hits theaters on December 18.

Maisler is a titan of casting, having worked on hundreds of films with filmmakers such as Luca Guadagnino, Greta Gerwig, Aaron Sorkin, Paul Greengrass, Adam McKay, and Terrence Malick, and she was nominated for the first casting Oscar in 2026 for her work on Ryan Coogler’s Sinners.

The casting Oscar didn’t exist when she began working on the Dune franchise, but this installment is likely to draw attention from the Academy. Over the three films, the cast has grown into an incredible ensemble, packed with many of today’s biggest movie stars, along with well-known veterans and a few unexpected choices. “One thing about Denis is if ever I bring him a name and he likes it, and I’ll say, ‘Well, do you want to hire that actor?’ He says to me something I think is so poetic,” says Maisler. “He says, ‘Francine, let me get back to you tomorrow. I need to dream about it.’”

Ahead of the release of Dune: Part Three, Maisler looks back at casting the trilogy’s most important roles, including the exciting new additions to the upcoming film—and the possibility of more Dune in the future.

In Herbert’s book, Atreides is a slender 15-year-old with dark hair. “To find a 15-year-old who had that talent to carry this whole movie, we weren’t sure was out there,” remembers Maisler. The name that came up was then 22-year-old Chalamet, whom Maisler had previously cast in Hostiles, Beautiful Boy, The King, and Little Women. Chalamet, who didn’t have to audition but did meet with Villeneuve, would have to play Atreides from a young man who then begins to amass power in the second film and, after a 12-year time jump, is burdened with the choices he’s made waging a galactic war in the third. Though Chalamet hadn’t led a big blockbuster before, Maisler saw the depth of his talent. “I do think Beautiful Boy showed me the depth of Timothée as an actor, as a young man, and that this was the next step in his progression as an actor, that he was able to hold a franchise in his hand,” says Maisler.

There was a worldwide search for Chani, the skilled Fremen warrior from Arrakis who falls in love with Atreides. At the time, Zendaya was in the middle of filming the first season of Euphoria, and her graduation from Disney star to movie star had not yet happened. Zendaya screen tested with Chalamet, which sealed it for Maisler and Villeneuve. “She came in with five other incredibly talented actresses, but the minute you saw her with Timothée in a room, you just knew that there’s something special happening,” she says. “She has such power when she walks in the room, and she’s breathtaking in the most interesting way.”

Of course, Paul Atreides’s parents, Duke Leto Atreides and Lady Jessica, needed to look like Chalamet, but Maisler started with the characters’ essences when casting. Duke Leto Atreides was considered a fair and devoted leader as the noble head of House Atreides. Maisler saw that gravitas in Oscar Isaac. Lady Jessica becomes a force in the story because of her heightened physical and mental control as a trained member of the Bene Gesserit sisterhood. “Rebecca is so powerful, isn’t she?” says Maisler. “She really, I have to say, surprised me. I always knew how talented she was, but she just owned that part.”

Villeneuve and Maisler had worked with Brolin on the 2015 crime thriller Sicario. Maisler, who calls Brolin “one of our greatest actors,” was excited to have him back, this time playing Gurney Halleck, the Warmaster of House Atreides and a mentor to Paul Atreides. The character is described in the book as a warrior-poet, requiring strength and depth. “He’s so charismatic, so masculine,” says Maisler of Brolin. “He’s kind of a throwback from other generations.”

When Momoa’s agent brought up Momoa’s name, Maisler wasn’t quite sure about the idea because at the time he was known for starring in the DC movie franchise as Aquaman. “I was a bit skeptical, I have to admit, because I knew he had this incredible presence on screen, but I didn’t know, truly, his talent, and that’s taught me a lot about being open to people who come from different types of films,” she says. Villeneuve was more open to the idea at the start, and met with him about playing Duncan Idaho, a fierce fighter and protector of Paul Atreides. He returns in the third movie as a ghola—a sort of clone—named Hayt, which demands a more complicated performance from Momoa. “Jason’s an incredible artist, and I’ve come to just love him,” says Maisler. “He’s so funny. I want to put him in a romantic comedy next, because he really is one of the big surprises in the ensemble.”

Taylor-Joy had already risen in stardom by the time she joined the franchise for the second film. Her breakout was in The Witch, and she starred in hit series The Queen's Gambit, which earned her a Golden Globe and a SAG Award. This made it slightly surprising that Alia Atreides, Paul’s volatile sister, makes a blink-and-you’ll-miss-it appearance in the second film. “I give her a lot of credit for not counting lines in the second one,” says Maisler, who says Taylor-Joy signed on for the second because of the potential of the third installment. Indeed, in Dune: Part Three, Alia is a loyal sister and vengeful force who is not afraid to get blood on her hands. Taylor-Joy’s charisma and intensity will jump off the screen, says Maisler. “Actors are very smart, and they know when to trust a director like Denis,” she says. “When he says there is going to be something in the third film and he describes it, he will make it happen.”

A tribal leader of the desert-dwelling Fremen, Stilgar is a seasoned warrior and becomes a devout follower of Paul Atreides as Muad’Dib. The role required a level of intensity. “Oh, I think we all just prayed that Javier would do it,” says Maisler. “I think every actor wants to work with Javier, and he’s one of probably a handful of actors I think can do anything.”

Pugh joined for the second film as well, but like Taylor-Joy, she didn’t have a ton to do. But Princess Irulan, who marries Paul Atreides as a political union, is a key part of the plot in Dune: Part Three, joining a conspiracy against Paul. Maisler first saw Pugh in the 2016 film Lady Macbeth, and then cast her as Amy March in Gerwig’s Little Women. “You saw on that what an intelligent actress she is, and singular,” she says. “She knows no boundaries, and she’s confident and bold.” She says Pugh has always reminded her of Debra Winger, the star of An Officer and a Gentleman (1982), and Terms of Endearment (1983). “She’s just commanding, and she has this energy, and everything she does is fascinating,” says Maisler. “You can’t take your eyes off of her.”

The third installment brings in yet another major star with Pattinson, who plays Scytale, a shape-shifter who is conspiring to dethrone Paul Atreides. Maisler, who also worked with Pattinson in Primetime, which also came out this year, describes him as “one of the versatile actors in his choices.” She had also worked with Pattinson on Mickey 17, which proved that he could play many different versions of a character—a skill that would be required of him in this third Dune movie. “Robert's a tremendous actor, and I think he takes these really bold chances,” says Maisler. As for his recent announcement as the next James Bond, Maisler has faith he and Villeneuve will deliver. “I think the way Denis and Rob created the character in Dune: Part Three together speaks to the surprises that we will see in Bond,” she says.

For Dune: Part Three, Maisler and Villeneuve had to find two actors who looked like twins and also looked like the offspring of Chalamet and Zendaya. They initially hoped to cast real twins, but didn’t find the right pair. In the end, they found their Ghanima and Leto II in Ida Brooke and Nakoa-Wolf Momoa. Brooke, who looks strikingly like Zendaya, is a relative newcomer who previously appeared on Apple’s sci-fi drama Silo (which stars Rebecca Ferguson). And Nakoa-Wolf Momoa, who makes his feature acting debut in Dune: Part Three, is Jason Momoa’s son—though Maisler didn’t know that when she first watched his audition tape. “Then came this tape of this young man who had incredible presence, and—we didn’t ask for this—he added some combat footage to his tape,” she says. Maisler says sometimes actors will call in a favor to get their child an audition, but Wolf, as she calls him, got this on his own. This casting was the most important for the third film because of what might be to come. “It was almost like casting the first one where these two young actors could go on to potentially, if there’s another movie where they’re leads,” says Maisler. There have been no official announcements of any future Dune movies, but for those mourning the end of the Villeneuve trilogy, Maisler is planting a small seed of hope here. The third Dune book, Children of Dune, centers on Leto and Ghanima, which means the two young actors Maisler found may have more story ahead of them.

#3401. The Best Early Tech Deals From Walmart’s 2026 Black Friday and Cyber Monday Sale

The first of Walmart's three major sales for Black Friday and Cyber Monday is now live, and there are already some amazing tech deals to take advantage of. I've gathered my top 10 tech products from the sale to make your life a little easier. For more, keep tabs on our Black Friday coverage, where we post the latest deals from not just Walmart, but Amazon, Best Buy, and other retailers' Black Friday deals.

Apple's latest smartwatch is the Series 12, but don't count out the Series 11. By sacrificing a few of Apple's newest features, you can save some money on the more premium version of this last-gen Apple Watch. Right now, the Titanium Series 11 GPS + cellular model is on sale for $429.

During WWDC 26 earlier this summer, Apple announced new Siri AI upgrades with watchOS 27—but only some Apple Watches have compatibility. Luckily, the Series 11 is one of them, at least for many of them. Some other upgrades in the new OS include a dedicated Siri app, a new app grid, a new single-tap gesture, among other features. Just note that only Series 12 and Ultra 4 can run Audio Intelligence.

The Garmin vivoactive 5 was $299.99 when it first came out in 2023 as their midrange lifestyle-focused fitness smartwatch. It features a 1.2-inch AMOLED touchscreen and an 11-day battery life (four to five days with the always-on display setting). You can get it for $169.99 right now. It's a great option for anyone looking to get into Garmin for the first time or upgrading from anything below it.

Bone conduction headphones are ideal for activities where it is vital to be able to hear your surroundings. They use a technology that sends audio vibrations to your inner ear while leaving your ear canals open. Shokz is one of, if not the best, brands making bone conduction headphones right now. At the high end of Shokz's offerings sit the OpenRun Pro 2, which impressed me when I tested them out for review. Walmart currently has a restored pair for $95 (originally $135.95 and $179.99 new).

The latest AirPods Pro are a big step up. The third iteration of Apple's iconic earbuds comes with a number of quality-of-life and software improvements that make them worth the typical premium over the AirPods Pro 2—and right now, the AirPods Pro 3 are even cheaper than the previous generation. They're $179 on Walmart as an early Black Friday deal, down from $249 and matching their lowest price ever.

Most, if not all, TV speakers aren't great. While you have plenty of options, the quickest and least expensive way to improve your TV's audio capabilities is to buy a soundbar. Compare a soundbar's size to the thin, small speakers jammed into modern TVs. The Vizio 4.1 Pro Soundbar and rear speakers come with Dolby Atmos support and cost just $79 (originally $148). They won't win any audio awards, but it's better than any built-in TV speakers, and for $79, it'll improve your experience without breaking the bank.

If you want to take things up a notch, consider this 5.1 channel sound system. Not only does it include far more channels than a single soundbar, but you're also adding a dedicated subwoofer to the mix. A subwoofer will make those thuds, explosions, and low vibrations much more pronounced than on a soundbar alone. For $149.99 (originally $249.99), you can get the ULTIMEA 5.1 surround sound system, which comes with a soundbar—replicating left, right, and center channels—two rear speakers, and a subwoofer.

I love projectors and Roku. To me, a Roku projector just makes sense, especially at $119.99 (originally $389.99). This projector is portable and has the Roku OS already installed, so it's easy to project it against a wall, ceiling, or screen, whether it's indoors or outdoors. It's easy to set up; you just need an outlet nearby and to dim or turn off the lights. If you have Bluetooth speakers, you can hook them up to create a more immersive sound.

The TCL Q51GB is a QLED Google TV that is a great value for anyone looking for size, color, and features. The 98-inch class is heavily discounted at its $898 price (originally $1,499.99). TCL makes one of the best QLEDs for the money, and their technology keeps getting better. This TV supports Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos, and if you're a gamer, you get a refresh rate of 240Hz that is automatically triggered with its Auto Game Mode feature.

Gaming monitors can get pricey fast. At $159.99 (originally $299.99 at launch), this 27-inch Samsung Odyssey G55C curved gaming monitor offers a 1440p resolution, a 1000R curve, a 165Hz refresh rate with FreeSync and G-SYNC compatibility to keep screen tearing to a minimum, and features like Samsung’s Virtual Aim Point and Contrast Enhancer. It's a solid choice for gaming, especially at this price point.

Alienware makes great gaming laptops, and the Aurora is a great option for anyone who wants to get all the essentials without spending too much. At its current $1,099 price (originally $1,999), the Alienware Aurora 16 becomes a mid-tier gaming laptop at a "budget" price. We reviewed the higher-tier Aurora 16X and were impressed with it. The Aurora 16 has a slightly slower processor, a dimmer display with half the refresh rate, a smaller battery, and a weaker graphics card, but given its price, it's great for a gamer looking for a solid gaming laptop in the $1,000 range.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Yes. Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Home Depot will all have in-store deals, some of which you might not find online, so if you're able to take a trip to your local retailer, keep your eyes open for different deals.

Amazon has a much larger inventory of tech products on sale, but the ones they both sell are mostly priced the same. While Amazon may have more deals, Walmart usually has a couple of surprise flagship tech products on sale that Amazon will later price match. So taking all of that into consideration, the best one will be whichever has whatever you're looking to buy at the lower price.

#3399. One Element Of Avengers: Doomsday Has Me Excited Above All Else

"Avengers: Doomsday" is going to be one of the biggest movies of the year, if not ever, that much is certain. But so far, the movie's marketing has been quite, well, underwhelming. We already had one "Avengers" film (well, two) that relied entirely on gathering lots of known Marvel Cinematic Universe characters on screen at the same time. To do that again feels less special, as exciting as it is to see Cyclops (James Marsden) leading the X-Men into battle here.

Indeed, the worst thing one can say about this film right now is that it looks exactly like what you would expect. It's massive, sure, but it doesn't feel surprising in any way. Marvel announcing Robert Downey Jr. as Doctor Doom in the movie felt desperate, too, as it was obviously the studio's way of trying to win back the fans who'd been disappointed by the MCU's post-"Avengers: Endgame" output. "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" aside, Marvel's no longer the reliable hit machine that it once was.

That being said, there is one notable reason to be excited about "Doomsday." No, not the X-Men (though their inclusion is certainly cool) or the return of Scarlet Witch (Elizabeth Olsen). Instead, it's the fact that "Doomsday" is technically a direct sequel to "Thunderbolts*," itself by far the best non-"Spider-Man" MCU movie since "Endgame." More specifically, it picks up where that film left off, with the titular team (also known as the West Chesapeake Valley Thunderbolts sponsored by Shane's Tire Company) now officially being known as the New Avengers.

Sure enough, the final "Doomsday" trailer features a few shots of the New Avengers amidst all the new footage of Chris Evans as Steve Rogers, and it's enough to finally get me hyped for this film.

For the most part, the visuals in the final "Avengers: Doomsday" trailer look horrendously muted and dull, save for a single brief shot of David Harbour's Alexei Shostakov dressed in a horrendous New Avengers tracksuit staring in awe as Shang-Chi (Simu Liu) arrives at Avengers Tower. Immediately, the image both brightens the trailer and reminds you that as serious as "Doomsday" may be (with the old Avengers looking more tired and beaten up than ever), the New Avengers bring a whole different vibe to the table. After all, they're silly, not great at teamwork, and don't consider themselves to be gods. Instead, they talk through their psychological issues and even hug it out like something out of "Neon Genesis Evangelion."

As the final trailer makes clear, "Doomsday" is all about different superhero groups coming together. You have the remnants of the original Avengers team, the X-Men, the Thunderbolts/New Avengers, and the Fantastic Four — plus the stragglers from various MCU titles that we collectively kind of forgot about. Each brings a different dynamic to the film, with the New Avengers specifically being a group of loser superheroes and criminals not unlike the Guardians of the Galaxy ... with the big difference being that the former have to save themselves before they can save anyone else. It's why "Thunderbolts*" makes for such an emotional gut punch, especially when its leads come together as a team, and the idea of seeing them interact with the MCU at large does more to make "Doomsday" feel interesting than any number of cameos could.

"Avengers: Doomsday" will see the New Avengers suit up alongside their companions when it hits theaters on December 18, 2026.

#3397. Decoding Kate Middleton’s “Tourdrobe” for Her Trip to India

When Kate Middleton stepped out on the green carpet at the Earthshot Awards ceremony in Mumbai this week, it was “an absolute princess moment,” says British designer Amanda Wakeley.

“Catherine has really come into her own. She has found her stride and a new confidence, and you see that in this dazzling but also practical ‘tourdrobe,’’’ Wakeley, who has previously dressed the Princess of Wales and used to dress Princess Diana, tells Vanity Fair.

It has been 10 years since Princess Kate last visited India. Her fashion choices are more sophisticated now than on her visit in 2016, and the speech she delivered at the Earthshot Prize ceremony on November 17 shows a new confidence. With her elevated look, there’s no trace of High Street labels. Kate’s flared floral dresses and the wedge shoes she used to love (but the late Queen Elizabeth apparently disliked) have been replaced by Manolo Blahnik pumps, couture power suits, and clothes by some of her favorite designers, such as Emilia Wickstead.

Prince William and Princess Kate attend The Earthshot Prize Awards Ceremony at the Jio World Convention Centre on November 17, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

Kate’s decision to wear a striking vermilion dress made from handwoven silk by New Delhi–based designer Mahima Mahajan to the Earthshot Prize ceremony spoke volumes. The eye-catching dress, which she paired with a burgundy Prada velvet clutch, was chosen after Kate had selected a special suite of emeralds from the royal gem collection. The green stones on the dress perfectly matched her jewels, which served as an homage to both Queen Elizabeth II and India, as the green of the Indian flag represents growth and prosperity.

The dazzling stones known as the “emerald tassel suite” were worn frequently by the late Queen Elizabeth II, and while Kate has previously worn the earrings, this marked the first time she wore the set. The effect was dramatic.

“Never has Catherine looked more like a queen in waiting,” Wakeley says of the look.

Wearing the suite ensured that Kate, who has free rein of the royal jewels, looked more regal than ever. “What was fascinating was seeing Catherine wear these incredible family heirlooms along with more relaxed collections from some of her favorite modern jewelry designers like Kiki McDonough and Astley Clarke,” remarks Wakeley.

Kate’s carefully curated wardrobe for the trip wasn’t just about power dressing—it was also about showing she can be sustainable as well as on trend.

“It was good to see Catherine making a proper nod to sustainability by rewearing her Roksanda dress,” Wakeley notes. “It’s clear a lot of thought has gone into her outfit choices. Her wardrobe has to be practical, and her clothes have to work harder than most people consider for their clothing; she needs weight in the hem of the floaty dresses. She has learned lessons the hard way. She is often seen bending down, talking to children, so she’s conscious of how low a neckline is, how short a skirt is.”

Princess Kate visits the Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital, on November 18, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

For her visit to Mumbai’s Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital on November 18, Catherine chose a striking red tailored Emilia Wickstead skirt suit with Manolo Blahnik pumps. On November 16, she opted for a pistachio blazer by designer Veronica Beard, paired with white Alexander McQueen trousers and pearl-buckled Camilla Elphick flats, a relaxed and accessible look for when she picked up a cricket bat.

Princess Kate plays cricket on November 16, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

As Princess of Wales, Catherine is often compared to Princess Diana. “The main difference is Diana was a fashion icon. Catherine has become a style icon,” Wakeley says. “There’s a big difference. Diana played into the fashion of the day and was finding her style. During the time she resigned from public life, she worked out her style DNA. Catherine has had to do that on the job. Very wisely, she has worked out her style and doesn’t get too impacted by fashion and trends. She goes for what she likes. What works for her rather than trends. She really knows now what works for her.”

Disneyland live entertainment is few and far between as of late, which is a shame considering the Anaheim theme park used to boast some of the best shows. On November 21st, one of the last and most beloved nighttime shows, Fantasmic, went up in flames for the second time in three short years. With two incidents and Disney’s desire to cut back on live entertainment, I’m really starting to worry about the future of the show.

The fire reportedly broke out during Fantasmic’s second performance of the night shortly before the show’s finale. While the Mark Twain finale was able to go on, flames can be seen behind the boat on the small stage set up on Tom Saywer Island. Guests at the park were quick to pull out their phones and film the growing flames as the Mark Twain, full of classic Disney characters, made its way around the river. Take a look:

Here’s the Mark Twain Riverboat running during Fantasmic last night with the fire behind it. This happened during the 10:30PM show https://t.co/bMcOZ6z0PtNovember 22, 2026

The last two minutes of the show were canceled, and guests were asked to vacate the viewing area while the fire department handled the blaze. Thankfully, the fire was small compared to the 2023 incident that turned the Maleficent dragon animatronic into a giant fireball and forever changed the show. There’s been no word on the extent of the damage this time around, but considering the show was back Sunday night it safe to assume that nothing was affected and no cast members were harmed, thankfully.

Two fiery incidents are definitely a cause for concern, and with Disneyland executives’ history of scaling back entertainment to cut costs, I can’t help but worry about the show’s fate. After all, Fantasmic boasts a large cast of incredible performers and several floating units. Plus water screens, projectors, and fireworks. I’m no expert, but I’m willing to bet it’s one of the most costly attractions at Disneyland. Not to mention, the show is still feeling the loss of the Maleficent Dragon, which makes the battle between Mickey and Maleficent lackluster.

While I don’t think Disneyland would end the show without also announcing a replacement, I do think Disney fans should prepare themselves. After all, Disney fans aren’t known for taking new changes well. Just look at the uproar that happened when it was announced Dinosaur would close to make room for a new Indiana Jones attraction at Disney World.

Disneyland has been having a rough go at things this month. On the first day of the holiday season, the Anaheim theme park’s iconic fake snow was accidentally turned on during a rainstorm, creating a mess. Back in October, Frontierland experienced widespread flooding. With park tickets being so expensive, it’s unfortunate to see cracks in Disneyland’s magic, but not even the mouse can control the weather or unexpected fires.

#3395. Steven Spielberg's Next Movie Is A Star-Studded Western Written By Another Legendary Filmmaker

Earlier this year, Steven Spielberg announced that his next movie as a director would be a Western. This will be his first official crack at the most American of film genres, and that's reason enough for cinephiles to get excited.

Now, Deadline has revealed that the movie, an adaptation of Kevin Barry's novel "The Heart in Winter," will star Cillian Murphy, Jessie Buckley and Mark Rylance, and it's hard not to be elated. Factor in that Barry's book is being adapted into a script by Oscar-winner Paul Thomas Anderson, and there isn't a word in the English language to capture the utter exhilaration movie fans are feeling at this moment.

No one's more enthused than Spielberg, though. As he told Deadline:

"It's really the excitement for me to get to work together with my dear friend and colleague Paul Thomas Anderson on a genre, but more particularly, the genre notwithstanding, a story that quite quickly became close to both our hearts and we felt that we could do as a team."

Murphy will play Tom Rourke, an Irish immigrant eking out a living in Butte, Montana. He works as an assistant to a photographer and supplements his income by penning letters for illiterate miners seeking potential brides from the east. He needs the extra scratch, too, due to his alcohol and opium addictions. Tom is spiritually adrift until mail-order bride Polly Gillespie arrives in Butte. They fall fast in love, steal some money, and set what proves to be an eventful course for San Francisco.

Overall, Barry's book has echoes of Spielberg's theatrical directing debut on "The Sugarland Express," as it's about two lovers on the run from the law. But this being the late 1800s, and the pair being challenged as horseback riders, their journey isn't quite as fast-paced.

Kevin Barry's "The Heart in Winter" has been described as "a tragedy written as farce" (per The Guardian). Critics found it hilarious and wildly entertaining, and after his excellent work on "One Battle After Another," I can't imagine anyone more suited to a tale about a character with an opium addiction stealing a mail-order bride and heading to San Francisco than Paul Thomas Anderson. But what's most interesting to me is that this will be the first time Anderson has written an entire script for another filmmaker. He previously did rewrites on the Apple-backed "Killers of the Flower Moon" and "Napoleon" for Martin Scorsese and Ridley Scott, but he's the primary writer here.

As for Steven Spielberg, no filmmaker alive knows more about Western conventions than him, and you can rest assured he will aggressively avoid cliché. I mean, he'll be sure to keep the horizon line out of the middle of the frame, lest John Ford's eye-patched ghost haunt him for the rest of his days, but don't expect traditional Western violence of the shootout and saloon brawl variety. I haven't read the book yet, so I don't know if such scenes exist in Barry's novel, but if they do, they'll look unlike any shootout or brawl you've ever seen.

What's curious is that Spielberg went with the Montana-set "The Heart in Winter," given that he'd been talking about making a Texas Western. Texas is not Montana by a long shot, which makes me wonder if he might change the location of Barry's novel. I doubt he'd do that, so now he's cheesed off everyone in Texas who was hoping he'd make their state look sensationally epic. He'll have to make it up to them somehow.

#3394. Steven Spielberg Officially Takes On a New Genre for Next Movie

Cillian Murphy and Jessie Buckley are heading to the Wild West in a new film from the legendary director

Steven Spielberg is finally getting his chance to make a Western, and he's bringing some serious star power along for the ride. The legendary filmmaker is developing an adaptation of The Heart in Winter, with Jessie Buckley (Hamnet), Cillian Murphy (Oppenheimer), and Mark Rylance (Bridge of Spies) set to star.

As reported by Deadline, Spielberg will direct the movie for Focus Features, with an adapted screenplay by Paul Thomas Anderson (One Battle After Another). The project is based on Kevin Barry's novel of the same name and is expected to arrive in theaters sometime in 2028.

The story follows two star-crossed fugitives trying to find a place for themselves in the American West during the late 19th century. Spielberg and Anderson will also produce alongside Kristie Macosko Krieger and Sara Murphy.

Spielberg has spoken about wanting to direct a Western for years, and the opportunity to collaborate with Anderson was a major draw. Speaking to Deadline, the director said the story quickly became close to both filmmakers' hearts, making it a project they wanted to tackle together.

The collaboration is particularly notable because Anderson is writing the screenplay without directing the film himself for the first time. The filmmaker recently won an Oscar for Best Adapted Screenplay for One Battle After Another, making him an especially intriguing choice to bring Barry's novel to the screen.

Spielberg also revealed that Buckley and Murphy were his first choices for the two central roles, saying they were the only actors he could imagine playing the characters. The pair have never appeared in a film together before.

Production is expected to begin in the winter of 2027, according to Deadline. Spielberg also made clear that the Western isn't intended to be his final film, joking that if he wanted to ride off into the sunset, he would have made Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade his final movie.

#3393. 10 Books Like ‘Dungeon Crawler Carl’ You Should Read Next

Jeff Somers is a freelancer who has been writing about writing, books, personal finance, and home maintenance since 2012.

Jeff has published nine novels and more than 70 short stories; his story Ringing the Changes was selected for inclusion in The Best American Mystery Stories 2006. In 2018, Jeff published the book Writing Without Rules: How to Write & Sell a Novel Without Guidelines, Experts, or (Occasionally) Pants. He holds a bachelor’s degree in English and previously worked in medical publishing as a production editor.

When not writing, Jeff spends his free time fixing up his old house. He has tackled a wide range of DIY projects, including remodeling a bathroom entirely on his own in two weeks, and building a roof deck that hasn't fallen down yet. You can find him on Bluesky.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

There’s nothing quite like Dungeon Crawler Carl, Matt Dinniman’s hilarious, inventive, and surprisingly emotional book series about a man in his underwear forced to fight his way through a livestreamed game show based on dungeon-crawling video games that takes place after an alien takeover of Earth. (Did I mention he's accompanied by his ex-girlfriend’s suddenly talkative cat?)

The premise should not work, but it sure does—and it makes more sense if you know it fits into a popular genre known as "LitRPG," a blend of "literature" and "role-playing game." If you've torn through all eight books released so far and you're looking for more reads that blend surprisingly deep hilarity with tabletop and video game rules (or just similar feels), here are 10 books you should check out.

An isekai story that lands in the sweet spot for DCC fans, He Who Fights with Monsters kicks off with Jason—a completely normal, kind of boring middle manager—waking up in a strange hedge maze, completely nude (even his hair is gone). He has magic that works like a video game, and has to deal with quests that slowly give him clothes (it’s a relief when he finally acquires some pants), force him to survive cannibals, and hunt down various monsters that definitely need killing. It’s got the same “gaming rules” structure as DCC and a similarly absurdist tone, with just the right spice of darkness.

The Cradle series by Will Wight isn’t a LitRPG, and it doesn’t have Carl’s focus on humor, but it’s another progression fantasy with enough game-like elements to be a great match. Lindon is an “unsouled,” incapable of gaining any of the sacred arts and doomed to a life without a future. His lack of power makes Lindon ferociously determined to find an alternative path to power and success, and that’s what drives this story. He has to find creative ways to move forward, and slowly this leads him to a path that just might make him the most powerful person in his world. DCC fans will love the progression and the tone.

One of the key elements of any video game is the respawn—you get killed, but you pop back up to try again, sometimes at the beginning, sometimes at a save point. Django Wexler leverages that mechanic to great effect in How to Become the Dark Lord and Die Trying. Davi has been summoned to a fantasy world to be the hero, the person who defeats the Dark Lord and saves the day—but she’s failed (and died) so many times, she’s fed up, and decides that on this run through, she’s going to switch sides and become the Dark Lord, using all her knowledge gained from endless replays to her advantage. The humor is pitch-black the way DCC fans like it, and the progressive structure is a perfect fit.

Is Princess Donut your favorite part of Dungeon Crawler Carl? Of course she is. In that case, check out Andrew Seiple’s Threadbare series. Threadbare is a stuffed bear brought to magical life in a failed experiment. He’s a foot tall, full of stuffing, and extremely dumb when the story begins. But when he’s rescued by a little girl and plunged into a horrible series of dangers, Threadbare has to find a way to level up. Like DCC, Threadbare starts off leaning into the absurdity and humor, then slowly gains emotional gravitas as the story progresses.

If you play tabletop RPGs, you’ve encountered a Murderhobo or two: A character who solves all their problems by killing—even members of their own party. Luke doesn’t aspire to be a Murderhobo—he just wants to take over the family business and hang with his buddies. But when an invasion threatens the kingdom, everyone over the age of 17 is ordered to be tested for Potential. Luke’s friends all test high and join the Ascender Corps, traveling to different planes for training. Luke tests ... very low, and when he steps through a portal to engage in his training, he finds himself without any guidance or training in a strange, deadly world where his only chance of survival is to murder his way through it. It’s dark, darkly funny, and a progression fantasy like no other.

If you’re looking for a book series that combines the dark, chaotic humor, absurd game mechanics, and surprising emotional depth of Carl, here’s Ryan “Quicksave” Romano, a man who has the unique ability to literally create a save point in his existence that allows him to go back and redo things whenever he dies. Searching for a childhood friend, he becomes embroiled in a violent gang war that lets him make good use of his power—but underneath the snark and the insanity of Ryan’s existence is a surprisingly affecting story of a man who has suffered, and suffered countless tragedies that are definitely taking their toll.

If your fave bit of DCC is Carl himself—a mediocre dude in an extraordinary situation—you should read Dennis E. Taylor’s fantastic Bobiverse books. Bob is a software engineer who hits it big and promptly dies, waking up to discover a century has passed and he’s been repurposed as an AI controlling a space probe searching for new planets for humanity to inhabit. If he fails in his mission (and he’s not the only probe out there), he’ll be turned off for good. Luckily, he can make copies of himself, and he’s pretty smart. The humor here is smart and soaked in pop culture, making it a perfect match for DCC fans.

Want more of Carl’s absurdist humor? Mayor of Noobtown is the LitRPG you’re looking for. Jim dies and wakes up in a video game-esque universe and finds himself stuck in the zone designated for newbies—players with no experience, skill, or hope. The area fell out of the mainline progression mechanic a long time ago, so there doesn’t seem to be a way to gain power, and the monsters are not at all concerned about the unfairness of it all, so Jim has to figure out how to advance in a universe that seems designed to kill him (again).

If you want to lean into the meta side of things, check out Scathing Reviewer, written by an author who goes by the unusual pen name "BananaDragon." Liu Peijin is the author of a sprawling LitRPG web novel, and she’s used to the bad reviews and complaints from readers—and quite combative about it. When her books’ universe blossoms into a very dangerous new reality, she should be perfectly positioned to survive, having written the story in the first place. But her story becoming real also means her insufferable protagonist is real, and all those nasty critics are now passing judgment on her entire existence. It’s a dark, funny takedown of the entire genre itself, and DCC fans will love it.

If you want a story that parallels the dungeon crawling aspect of DCC, Andrew Rowe’s Arcane Ascension series is the ticket. The Serpent Spire is a tower of constantly changing traps, puzzles, and dangerous creatures. If you enter and survive, you emerge with magical powers. Corin Cadence’s brother entered the Serpent Spire years ago and never returned—and now Corin is determined not only to survive, but to make it to the top, where legend says a goddess will grant you whatever you wish. And what Corin wants is his brother back. It’s a literal progression combined with LitRPG rules, game-inspired puzzle-solving, and a complex magic system that fans of Carl will definitely enjoy.

#3392. 5 Reasons Why The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping Ruled The Box Office

The biggest YA franchise in the game is back on top. Lionsgate released "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" in theaters over the weekend, and to say that the franchise's latest prequel film did well would be an understatement. This movie is already a huge hit for the studio and has brought the property back to its former, $100 million-plus opening weekend glory.

Directed once again by franchise shepherd Franchise Lawrence, "Sunrise on the Reaping" opened to a massive $120 million domestically. Internationally, the prequel bowed to $105 million, giving it a gigantic $225 million global start. It's now Lionsgate's biggest opening of 2026 overall. "Michael" ruled the box office with a $218 million global opening earlier this year, but "Sunrise on the Reaping" even managed to best the King of Pop. Now, whether or not this movie gets to the $1 billion mark like "Michael" in the long run is another question entirely, but it illustrates just how big this opening was.

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" looked like it was going to be a bigger hit than people realized, which proved true. It arrived right in line with bullish estimates, which climbed through the roof in the weeks leading up to its arrival. As such, it's now poised to become one of the biggest hits of the year overall.

So, what went right here? How did Lionsgate manage to make such a big bet and have it pay off so spectacularly well? We're going to look at the biggest reasons why "Sunrise on the Reaping" ruled the box office on its opening weekend. Let's get into it.

The biggest thing that this movie had going for it is that it wasn't just another "Hunger Games" film or a prequel for the sake of a prequel. It was a story that hardcore fans of the franchise have been waiting a long time to see. Specifically, one involving the famed games where Haymitch Abernathy, the character played by Woody Harrelson in the previous "Hunger Games" movies, won.

"Sunrise on the Reaping" pits a young Haymitch (Joseph Zada) against President Snow (Ralph Fiennes), to put it in the simplest possible terms. "Hunger Games" author Suzanne Collins wrote the book the movie is based on and, rather crucially, the novel was received very well by fans. And by most accounts, Francis Lawrence, with the help of Collins, delivered one heck of an adaptation. All of this to say, the movie promised something fans had been wanting for a hot minute and delivered the goods when the time arrived.

Beyond that, Jennifer Lawrence also broke her silence on her "Hunger Games" return in "Sunrise on the Reaping" ahead of the film's release, assuring that this movie was getting the original gang back together. That undoubtedly helped get more casual viewers on board who perhaps were only more interested in the original set of "Hunger Games" films. Overall, Lionsgate made the most of what this story had to offer, turning it into not just another movie but a true event within one of the biggest franchises of the last 20 years — one that demanded to be seen on the biggest screen available as soon as possible.

This is the kind of movie that hardcore fans were always going to be in the bag for, no matter what. That having been said, positive word of mouth never hurts. And while critics were, more or less, on this film's side, it worked like gangbusters for the intended audience. In the case of a long-running, beloved franchise, that is always more important.

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" holds a decent 69% critical approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, as of this writing. However, it carries a stellar 94% audience score, which is near-universal praise from actual ticket buying fans. It also earned a damn good A- CinemaScore, which means word of mouth is going to be great in the weeks to come. Even though "Focker In-Law" could be a rare comedy box office hit over Thanksgiving, with Disney's "Hexed" opening as well, there should be more than enough room for this prequel to have a stellar second frame over the holiday weekend.

/Film's Nina Starner wrote that "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is a prequel that "delivers" in her review. Certain critics may have been a bit softer on it, but enough of them liked it to prevent the needle from being pushed down. More importantly, fans are loudly proclaiming their love for this film, which is going to do way more to motivate viewers who might have been on the fence to check it out in the coming weeks.

Lionsgate doesn't always have a lot of success when playing in the big-budget realm, but this franchise has generally been the exception to that rule. All of "The Hunger Games" movies have been hits at the box office and, save for the very first film, they've all benefited from November releases. This ended up being an "if it ain't broke, don't fix it" situation. All the same, the studio wisely picked the perfect spot on the calendar for this prequel to thrive.

Word of mouth can't be predicted, but getting in on an otherwise fairly dead pre-Thanksgiving weekend was very wise. "Sunrise on the Reaping" got one totally unimpeded weekend to do its thing and will now benefit from a long, five-day holiday weekend over Thanksgiving. It's basically going to have nine full days of ruling the box office before taking any sort of meaningful hit.

"The Hunger Games: Mockingjay — Part 2" ruled the box office in 2015, also in November, delivering a $102 million opening weekend en route to $653 million worldwide. This latest prequel had an even bigger opening, meaning it could eclipse that global figure when all's said and done. Not to get too ahead of ourselves, but it may wind up closer to "Mockingjay — Part 1" ($766 million worldwide), if all goes well.

Wherever the chips fall at the end of the day, it's going to be in large part because this movie wasn't competing with a slew of other blockbusters in the midst of a crowded summer. This is the big cinematic event of choice right now and will be for at least a couple of weeks.

It certainly doesn't happen too often, but if a franchise gets it right, the breakout sequel effect can come into play. One of the best examples in history is "The Dark Knight." While Christopher Nolan's "Batman Begins" was actually a bit of a box office disappointment, pulling in a so-so $373 million worldwide, "The Dark Knight" was simply too good to be ignored and made $1 billion at a time when movies rarely ever hit that milestone.

Other examples include "John Wick"/"John Wick: Chapter 2" and "Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse/"Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse." A very good first movie happened, people caught up with it after the fact, and that resulted in a much larger audience for the sequel. That brings us back to "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping." Despite being the sixth entry in this property, it benefited like a breakout sequel would have.

2023's "The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes" was a surprise victor at the Thanksgiving box office, ultimately pulling in nearly $350 million worldwide on a $100 million budget. A solid result, but it wasn't nearly what the first four movies in the "Hunger Games" franchise made. However, audiences and fans caught up with it and ended up enjoying it. So, after an eight-year break, Lionsgate kind of used that first prequel to prime the pumps on this franchise, even if that wasn't the intention.

The end result is that "Songbirds & Snakes" teed up the ball for "Sunrise on the Reaping," paving the way for the film to enjoy a much, much bigger opening than its predecessor. It's not a traditional breakout sequel, but it's a breakout sequel to a prequel people enjoyed.

Perhaps the most important factor when it comes to playing Monday morning quarterback with the success of "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" has to do with how big franchises are typically handled in Hollywood these days. Spin-offs. TV shows. Animated entries. Theme parks. More merchandise than anyone knows what to do with.

That never really happened with "The Hunger Games." That's in no small part because author Suzanne Collins has a lot of say over how those affairs are handled. Even so, there was an eight-year gap between movies by the time "The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes" came around and another three years before "Sunrise on the Reaping." Neither Lionsgate nor Collins ever allowed for overexposure to get the best of this franchise. That allowed for people to be legitimately excited about this film.

Former Disney CEO Bob Iger even admitted that multiple Marvel shows and Pixar movies going to streaming hurt those brands. The Marvel Cinematic Universe is mighty, but even fans grew tired of that. Likewise, Pixar is as good as cinema gets, yet audiences learned that they could just watch those movies at home. Meanwhile, Lionsgate has maintained discipline with the "Hunger Games" films and ensured that they remained cinematic events. Short-term gains and overdoing it would have potentially kneecapped what is now one of the studio's biggest hits in years. Hollywood could stand to learn a thing or two from this sort of execution.

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is in theaters now.

#3390. As Abbott Elementary Fans Hope For Janine And Gregory’s Engagement At Disneyland, I Have A Question

For six seasons now, Abbott Elementary fans have faithfully watched the relationship between Janine Teagues (Quinta Brunson) and Gregory Eddie (Tyler James Williams) progress. The pair have gone from good friends to committed lovers over the past several years and, now, it seems we’re on the cusp of a proposal. Many viewers are hoping an engagement will come during the Disneyland-set 100th episode that’ll air amid the 2026 TV schedule. I’d love that as well, but I also have a question about two other characters.

Gregory and Janine are, of course, the core couple on Abbott, but plenty of other romantic relationships amongst characters have been highlighted as well. As we anticipate what lies ahead for Janine and Gregory, I can’t help but wonder what the future holds for Ava Coleman and O’Shon, who’ve been dating since Season 4. I’ve enjoyed seeing their relationship develop as well as the funny moments that have resulted from that. With that, it’s hard not to wonder what the long-term plan for them might look like.

It’s clear that the affable O’Shon (Matthew Law) and Abbott’s diva of a principal Ava (Critics Choice winner Janelle James) are on steady footing after some initial growing pains. At this point, the pair have not only vacationed together, but they’ve also reached the point where they can throw a party as a couple. (That Halloween shindig they held this season was fantastic). Some may think it’s a bit early to consider a proposal for these two, but I don’t think it’s wild to think it could happen by the end of Season 6.

Gregory first expressed interest in proposing to Janine at the end of Season 5, which was about two years after the two finally got together. Ava and O’Shon will be reaching that mark later in the sixth season and, while great TV couples have different timelines, I could see O’Shon popping the question soon. Plus, given how encouraging O’Shon has been amid Gregory’s attempts to propose, who’s to say the former doesn’t want that for himself sometime in the near future?

Of course, I’m not saying anyone needs to be jumping the broom by the end of this season. I just wouldn’t mind seeing one or two engagements by the time Abbott’s finale rolls around next spring. That may seem like a long shot for Ava and O’Shon right now, but I’m feeling very good about Janine and Gregory’s chances of hitting that milestone.

The True Story That Inspired Abbott Elementary’s Choice To Move The School Into A Mall

Gregory has been trying to orchestrate the right moment to present Janine with a ring. During the show’s latest episode, “Competition,” he attempted to land a reservation at a popular Italian restaurant, where he could propose. Ironically, that plan became moot once Abbott’s Step Team punched their ticket to Disneyland, and Janine informed her man that they’d serve as chaperones on the trip. So it now seems like a given that Gregory will attempt to propose while he and his lady are in “The Happiest Place On Earth.”

What’s more is that the pressure is going to be on, as Janine is aware of her beau’s intention to pop the question (thanks to a major slip-up on Ava’s part). So the pressure is really on for Eddie to craft the perfect proposal. The Disneyland episode could indeed present him the right situation to do just that and, if Gregory does pull it off in great fashion, it might set a bit of a bar for O’Shon to clear if he eventually takes that step.

We’ll just have to wait and see how it plays out when Abbott Elementary airs its hundredth episode on Wednesday, December 2 at 8:30 p.m. ET on ABC. Fans can also stream the show the next day with a Hulu subscription.

Amazon's early Black Friday 2026 sale is already bringing substantial discounts to smart TVs, with savings ranging from $200 to $1,350 across models from Samsung, LG, Hisense, Sony, TCL, and other major brands. Several of the TVs included are from this year's lineups, so you don't necessarily have to settle for an older model to get a good price. There's also a decent variety to choose from, whether you're looking for an OLED TV with excellent contrast for movie nights, a bright mini-LED display for a sunlit living room, or simply a bigger screen without spending a fortune.

We've rounded up some of the more interesting offers below, and you can check out the rest of our Black Friday coverage for more editor-vetted tech deals as the sale continues.

Samsung’s 65-inch S90H is down to $1,397.99 from $1,897.99, saving you $500 on the company’s mid-range OLED TV for 2026. It’s a solid option for movie enthusiasts and gamers alike, thanks to its self-lit pixels that produce deep blacks and excellent contrast, particularly in darker scenes where conventional LED TVs can struggle with a grayish glow. You also get a high-refresh-rate display for smoother gaming.

If you have room for a bigger screen, Samsung’s 77-inch S85H is also worth a look, especially now that it’s down to $1,797.99 from $2,197.99, saving you $400. Although it sits below the S90H in Samsung’s 2026 OLED lineup, it still delivers the deep blacks, excellent contrast, and wide viewing angles that make OLED TVs appealing. The larger screen also makes it a good fit for family movie nights.

One of the biggest discounts in this roundup, the 2026 75-inch Hisense U7 is now $997.99, down from $1,999.99. Its mini-LED backlighting and local dimming are designed to deliver brighter highlights and better contrast, making it an appealing option for rooms with plenty of natural light. Gaming-focused features also make it worth a look if you plan to connect a current-generation console or gaming PC.

For a more affordable 75-inch option, Hisense's 2026 U6 Pro is down to $699.99 from $1,399.99, saving you $700. Like the U7, it uses mini-LED backlighting to improve contrast and bring out more detail in HDR movies and shows, although it sits a tier below the U7 in terms of overall picture performance. It also comes with Fire TV and Alexa+ built in, making it a convenient choice for households already using Amazon's smart home ecosystem.

The C6 is LG’s mid-range OLED evo model for 2026, and right now its 65-inch model is $1,399.99, down from its $2,699.99 launch price. It combines excellent pixel-level contrast with gaming features designed for fast-paced titles, making it a versatile choice for both movies and consoles. LG also supports Dolby Vision, which gives it an advantage over Samsung's OLEDs for viewers who regularly stream compatible HDR content.

Sony’s 65-inch Bravia 6, the entry-level OLED in its 2026 TV lineup, is now $1,198, down from $1,999.99, saving you $802. It delivers the deep blacks and excellent contrast you'd expect from the display technology, thanks to its self-lit pixels. Sony's picture processing also helps bring out fine details and natural-looking colors in movies and TV shows, while Dolby Vision support makes the most of compatible HDR content.

For the same $1,198, you can get a considerably larger screen with the 85-inch Sony Bravia 3 II, which is down from $1,599.99, saving you $402. That said, this 2026 model uses a conventional LED panel, so it won't quite match the Bravia 6's deep blacks and contrast, but the extra 20 inches make it an appealing option for sports and family movie nights. It also has a native 120Hz refresh rate with VRR and ALLM for smoother console gaming, along with Dolby Vision support and Google TV with Gemini built in.

Toshiba’s 75-inch Z670R is down to $699.99 from $1,299.99, saving you $600 on a 2026 mini-LED TV. It combines full-array local dimming with QLED color technology for improved contrast and brighter highlights, while Toshiba’s REGZA Engine ZRi processor helps sharpen lower-resolution content. The native 144Hz refresh rate also makes it a good option for console and PC gaming, and you get Fire TV built in for streaming, along with Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos support.

Designed to compete with Samsung's The Frame, Toshiba's 65-inch G700 ArtVision is currently $899.99 at Amazon, down from $1,297.99, saving you $398. It's a 4K QLED TV, with a native 165Hz refresh rate, built-in Fire TV, and the same REGZA Engine ZRi processor found in the Z670R. But there's more to it than watching movies and shows, as its Ambient Mode can display over 3,000 curated artworks without a subscription, while the matte anti-glare screen and included white oak frame help it pass for a framed print on the wall.

TCL’s 98-inch F8D is down to $1,444.99 from $1,699.99, saving you $255 on a massive 2026 QLED Fire TV. It uses a high-brightness LED backlight, so you won't get the same level of contrast control as TCL's more expensive mini-LED QM models, but it still offers a native 144Hz refresh rate for smoother gaming, along with Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos support. And at nearly 100 inches, there's plenty of screen space to make movies, sports, and games feel more immersive.

TCL’s 75-inch QM64L is down to $699.99 after a $200 price cut—it’s the cheapest way into TCL’s 2026 QD-Mini LED lineup, and it pairs quantum dot color with local dimming for brighter highlights and better contrast in HDR movies and sports. That also makes it a good pick for a bright living room, where an OLED might not be the most practical choice. You also get a native 144Hz refresh rate for gaming and Fire TV built in

Roku’s 65-inch Plus Series is the most affordable TV in this roundup at $449.99, down from $649.99, saving you $200. This 2025 model combines a QLED panel with mini-LED backlighting and Dolby Vision support for improved contrast and richer colors when watching HDR content. It also runs the same Roku OS found on the company’s streaming sticks and comes with an Enhanced Voice Remote, so navigating apps and finding something to watch should feel familiar to anyone who already uses Roku.

LG’s 65-inch C6 OLED has the largest dollar discount in this sale at $1,350 off, which brings it from $2,699.99 down to $1,349.99.

There's no guarantee that Cyber Monday will bring lower TV prices, particularly when some of the early Black Friday deals are already offering discounts approaching 50%. Retailers sometimes carry the same promotions through the entire shopping weekend, while others introduce new discounts or change which models are on sale.

That depends on your budget, room size, and how you plan to use it. The LG OLED evo C6 and Samsung S90H are worth considering for movie enthusiasts and gamers who want excellent contrast and smooth motion, while the Hisense U7 and TCL QM64L offer mini-LED alternatives for brighter living rooms. For a large screen at a relatively affordable price, the 75-inch Hisense U6 Pro at $699.99 stands out, while the 65-inch Roku Plus Series at $449.99 makes sense for everyday streaming on a tighter budget. If screen size is your priority, the 98-inch TCL F8D is also worth a look, provided you have the room for it.

#3388. Avengers: Doomsday Final Trailer Breakdown - 5 Biggest Reveals And What They Mean

The new "Avengers: Doomsday" trailer shows MCU heroes assembling for their biggest battle yet. It will also surely be one of their most profitable, given the hype around this movie. Despite Marvel Studios' well-publicized troubles of late, the Avengers' return remains highly anticipated. As such, any new revelations Marvel is willing to provide about the team-up movie are significant to say the least.

The final "Doomsday" trailer doesn't actually feature any major reveals, which is a good thing for those who prefer to keep their theater experience as pure as possible. For those who like to know as much as they can ahead of a Marvel Cinematic Universe release, however, it means much of the movie remains a mystery. (We're still no clearer on whether Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom is actually a Tony Stark variant or not, despite Marvel Studios head Kevin Feige's recent comments.) That said, the latest tease did contain several notable moments that have only served to increase the already significant hype.

The new "Doomsday" trailer finally gives Cyclops the X-Men line fans were waiting for, when Marsden's hero delivers his "To me, my X-Men" rallying cry to assemble his mutants, the Avengers, Fantastic Four, and several other heroes. But beyond that tantalizing glimpse at the film's big showdown, there are several other notable moments, and lucky for you, we've gone and rounded 'em up.

The precise plot of "Avengers: Doomsday" remains under wraps for now, but at this point, we can pretty much piece together the major beats. Previously, co-director Joe Russo told Empire that Robert Downey Jr.'s Victor Von Doom is a "father who's a victim of trauma" and that he "lost a child." That lined up with what we've seen in previous trailers, wherein Vanessa Kirby's Sue Storm/Invisible Woman talked about how Doom "used to be different" before "everything he loved was taken from him." Now, the latest "Doomsday" trailer has confirmed that the Avengers themselves are responsible for it all.

In the new trailer, Chris Evans' Steve Rogers can be heard saying, "Years ago, we did what was needed to make the world right," in reference to the events of 2019's "Avengers: Endgame." He continues: "But we didn't know those choices would have consequences." It seems that Steve's choice to travel back through time to be with his lover, Peggy Carter (Hayley Atwell) — and whatever the Avengers did to defeat Josh Brolin's Thanos — caused some sort of multiversal upheaval in which Doom's daughter met her, well, doom.

This is why RDJ's villain tells the heroes of "Doomsday" that they've been living "stolen lives." With Steve's speech in the new trailer, it's all but certain he and the Avengers are responsible for whatever killed Doom's daughter, and likely the multiversal collapse referenced in the "Avengers Endgame: Encore" TVA scene. Turns out, Doom is the "consequence" to which Steve refers.

Thanks to what seemed like a hasty casting announcement prior to the final "Avengers: Doomsday" trailer, we knew Hailee Steinfeld's Kate Bishop would be appearing in the movie. Now, the trailer has given us our first look at the heir to the Hawkeye mantle in a very quick shot that shows her looking up at something that's clearly got her very worried. But Kate might be just one of the Young Avengers to appear in the film.

We know Scott Lang's (Paul Rudd) daughter, Cassie Lang (Kathryn Newton), is also part of "Doomsday." She shows up briefly in the new trailer, too, looking as concerned as Kate. Interestingly enough, both characters are in their superhero suits, which suggests they'll be joining the big fight against Doctor Doom. That means two members of the Young Avengers will be involved in "Doomsday." Marvel Studios has yet to officially introduce these heroes as the superhero group from the comics, but has been slowly building up this new generation of Avengers over the past few years.

The only likely member of the Young Avengers who hasn't appeared in trailers and is yet to be confirmed as being involved with "Doomsday" is Iman Vellani's Ms. Marvel. According to Andy Serkis, Ms. Marvel will appear in "Doomsday," but Marvel hasn't made that official. Otherwise, there are a handful of other young heroes that could show up and potentially form the Young Avengers proper in the movie itself, including Riri Williams/Ironheart (Dominique Thorne) and America Chavez (Xochitl Gomez). For now, it looks more likely than ever we'll see an official Young Avengers group unite in "Doomsday."

The new "Avengers: Doomsday" trailer shows Chris Hemsworth's Thor rising from the floor surrounded by yellow lightning as opposed to his typical blue lightning. That's significant, as it all but confirms he'll be wielding a powerful new force known as the Odinforce. This power, created by the Kings of Asgard, is a major upgrade for the character, and the latest trailer appears to have shown it in action.

One of the most frequently showcased "Doomsday" scenes thus far has been the moment in which Thor launches himself at Doctor Doom, only to be stopped mid-air and flung backwards by the villain's formidable force (which, as it happens, involves a Jacky Kirby-inspired energy blast from Doom). Clearly, the God of Thunder is as outmatched as the rest of his cohorts.

But back when the first four teaser trailers for "Doomsday" dropped, we saw Hemsworth's hero begging his father for the "strength of the All-Fathers." Since then we've seen concept art and a "Doomsday" billboard that seemingly spoiled the fact Thor was getting a major upgrade in the form of the Odinforce. It's this force that turns his lightning yellow, and the final "Doomsday" trailer is the first time we see footage of it in action. The brief shot shows Thor ascending in a forest, which looks to be the same forest in which he begged for the strength of the All-Fathers in the original teaser. Looks like he got his wish. Whether it will prove effective against Doom, however, remains to be seen.

We got our first look at the X-Men in "Avengers: Doomsday" courtesy of the X-Men-heavy trailer back in January 2026. Since then, we've learned how the mutants might find their way to the Avengers. The film will take place during the collapse of the multiverse, whereby several "incursions" will see planets and timelines collide. These collisions are likely to be the reason for the film's major crossovers, i.e. the Fox-era X-Men and the Fantastic Four arriving on the Avengers' Earth 616. But it seems when the X-Men and Avengers first come face to face they initially clash, as evidenced by footage from prior trailers in which Yelena Belova/Black Widow (Florence Pugh) takes on Mystique (Rebecca Romijn) and Shang-Chi (Simu Liu) battles Gambit (Channing Tatum).

Now, however, the final "Doomsday" trailer has confirmed that Anthony Mackie's Sam Wilson/Captain America will face off against James Marsden's Scott Summers/Cyclops. The trailer shows the pair going toe-to-toe in what looks to be a pretty brutal clash, with Wilson holding Cyclops by the neck as he unleashes an optic blast. Clearly, the X-Men and Avengers ultimately manage to, as Thor puts it, "put aside their petty squabbles." But for at least a moment, the two superhero teams will be at odds in the movie, and Sam Wilson's showdown with Scott Summers looks set to be a major highlight.

The final "Avengers: Doomsday" trailer reminds us of the main threat facing Earth 616 in the movie. While Doctor Doom is the big bad, the entire multiverse is collapsing, and in the latest trailer we see a brief shot that shows two planets in the sky above New York City. The trailer also features several shots of heroes looking up at the sky, or out of windows and reacting with shock and dismay, and it's likely this planetary incursion is what has them so upset.

We've known that the heroes of "Doomsday" would be dealing with multiversal collapse in the film for some time. But this is the first shot we've seen in an official trailer that shows planets on a collision course with Earth. Previously, a Dunkin' Donuts commercial gave us our best look at the threat the Avengers face in "Doomsday," with a shot showing a planet looming in the sky over Avengers Tower. But it looks as though multiple timelines/planets are set to collide with Earth based on the brief scene from this latest trailer.

Exactly which planets these are remains unclear. One may in fact be the Fox-era X-Men's world, and this cityscape view could be giving us a glimpse of their arrival in the Avengers' timeline. Either way, clearly the stakes have never been higher, as failure means the complete and utter destruction of the multiverse.

"Avengers: Doomsday" hits theaters on December 18, 2026.

#3387. Prince William Reportedly Wants to Strip Prince Harry of His Titles

Prince William is reportedly actively considering a plan for a “far-reaching restructuring” of the British monarchy, which he would implement once he ascends to the throne. His brother, Prince Harry, would be at the forefront of these changes: The future monarch reportedly wants only active members of the royal family who carry out duties on his behalf to retain their royal titles and the style of “Royal Highness.” These titles would therefore no longer be an “automatic privilege of birth” but would instead be equivalent to a “job title.”

The plan was detailed by Tom Sykes, a journalist and writer specializing in the royals, in his book Dukes of Hazard, to be published next February, excerpts of which were published by the Mail on Sunday on Saturday, November 21. The author, “a royal authority with impeccable society contacts” as the newspaper puts it, is said to have obtained confessions from friends of Prince William.

“If you are a working royal—going out, touring the country, doing diplomatic work, doing government work, having a public role, pressing the flesh, getting out of bed on a wet Wednesday to go to Sheffield—then you will be an HRH and you will have a prince or princess title. You will also get an allowance, a salary, and a place to live. One place to live,” the associate of the prince explained to Sykes. “If you are not doing those things and you are not a working royal, you will not get to be an HRH, you will not get a free or subsidized place to live, and you will not get any special favors. You will, however, be a private citizen free to get on with your life and make money any way you choose.”

By implementing this measure, Prince William hopes to prevent potential media scandals regarding the legitimacy of certain individuals’ right to retain their titles if they are not prominent members of the Firm (Prince Harry) or if they are under legal scrutiny (Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor). But also, and above all, the Prince of Wales hopes to offer an option to his children, Princess Charlotte, 11, and Prince Louis, eight, who could easily renounce their titles to pursue independent careers. The question does not arise for the eldest child of the Prince and Princess of Wales, Prince George, 13, whose future as heir to the throne is “guaranteed.” In fact, none of the three use their royal titles, preferring simply to be called by their first names and the surname Wales.

Under the rules established by King George V in 1917, the title of prince or princess, along with the predicate, is granted at birth to the sovereign’s children and to the children of the sovereign’s sons, as well as to all the children of the Prince of Wales’s eldest son. Prince William’s children, therefore, received these titles at birth, while Prince Harry’s children, Archie and Lilibet (ages seven and five), did not become prince and princess until King Charles III ascended the throne.

They may have to give them up if Prince William carries out his plan. “Under William’s current plan, the prince and princess titles of Harry and Meghan’s children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, would be legally removed, along with the royal styles and princely titles of Harry and Meghan themselves,” writes Tom Sykes in his book. To do so, according to Sykes’s book, constitutional advisers have told William that he could issue letters patent, an official document authorized by the king. Such a decision could strain the relationship between the two brothers.

Sykes is convinced that Prince William would garner the approval of his subjects and “enormous public support in a country increasingly impatient with the cost and perceived excess of a sprawling royal household,” according to those close to him.

In October 2025, Prince William confided to actor Eugene Levy—whom he was hosting at Windsor Castle for the taping of Levy’s show The Reluctant Traveler—that “there are points when you look at tradition and go, Is that still fit for purpose today? Is that still the right thing to do? Are we still doing and having the most impact we could be having?”

Kensington Palace, however, declined to comment on the rumor. “As a matter of policy, we don’t comment on books or claims made within them.”

Originally published in Vanity Fair France.

#3386. Naruto Movie Officially Casts Fan-favorite Actor for Key Role

Director Destin Daniel Cretton has found his Hokage

Spider-Man: Brand New Day director Destin Daniel Cretton is gearing up for his next live-action adaptation of an iconic franchise. He's writing and directing a live-action Naruto movie, and is in the process of casting an important role.

On Monday, Deadline reported Hiroyuki Sanada is in "final negotiations" with Lionsgate to play the Third Hokage of the Hidden Leaf Village, Hiruzen Sarutobi. He's a compassionate leader who tries to look out for Naruto, and in his younger days he led a team of Jiraiya, Orochimaru, and Tsunade. Early in the series, he gets to show off his power as a shinobi in a battle against Orochimaru during the invasion of Konoha.

Hiroyuki Sanada is a renowned Japanese actor who gained prominence in Hollywood in the 2000s with roles in the Tom Cruise epic The Last Samurai and Rush Hour 3. He's joined more nerdy franchises than you can count, starring in Speed Racer, The Wolverine, Avengers: Endgame, John Wick: Chapter 4, and the 2020s Mortal Kombat movies as Scorpion. On TV, you've seen him in Westworld and Shōgun. He's a trained martial artist and demonstrates that skill every time he's on screen.

Sanada will join Charles Melton in the Naruto movie. Reports surfaced a few months ago that Cretton was eyeing Melton to play Naruto's teacher, Kakashi Hatake. The latest Deadline report notes that Melton is still in talks to star in the film.

Cretton announced a casting search for the Team 7 leads, Naruto, Sasuke, and Sakura, in July. His picture doesn't have a release date yet, but production will start in spring of next year.
