#3333. From ‘Disclosure Day’ to ‘Devil Wears Prada’: Emily Blunt Breaks Down 10 of Her Greatest Movie Moments

Jimmy Stewart once said that with movies, it’s key moments that people remember.

Emily Blunt, who’s on the circuit these days talking about her standout role as a language-spouting meteorologist in Steven Spielberg’s “Disclosure Day,” gave me some memorable scenes that she will never forget from her wide-ranging filmography. (We spoke on Zoom.)

Clearly, Blunt can deliver in any genre: romance, comedy, musical, sci-fi, action, thriller, drama. So far, Blunt has notched one Oscar nomination, for Supporting Actress in Christopher Nolan’s bio-drama “Oppenheimer.” Sci-fi thriller “Disclosure Day” could score Blunt’s first Best Actress nod. (More below.) Related Stories How Sound Design Helps ‘Minotaur’ Get Away with Murder Super Bowl LXI to Play Live on IMAX Screens

1. “My Summer of Love” (2005, Pawel Pawlikowski) was Blunt’s first movie role. “I remember the wildness of that Edith Piaf dance [‘La Foule’], where I have the cigarette dangling out of my mouth, and she’s trying to romanticize this girl from the wrong side of town and sophisticate her. I remember the scene with Paddy Considine where she tries to seduce him and then she laughs at him. I will never forget the energy in that room and how Paddy was in that scene. I have taken what Pawel taught me about ambiguity and reality on camera, and I have used it throughout my career. I am an untrained actor. I don’t have anything technical to fall back on, but the aliveness that he created on ‘My Summer of Love’ was informative for how I moved forward: what lies beneath the character. You know what the front foot is, and what is the shadow of that person? What’s really going on?”

2. “The Devil Wears Prada“ (2006, David Frankel) marked Blunt’s Hollywood breakout as Miranda Priestley’s beleaguered first assistant Emily Charlton. After she gets hit by a taxi, second assistant Andy Sachs (Anne Hathaway) visits her hospital room. Charlton is angry and tearful at everything she is missing. “The hospital scene makes me laugh because that’s really who she is: this completely broken down, vulnerable, insecure person.”

3. “The Young Victoria” (2010, Jean-Marc Vallée) gave Blunt a queen to embody. “I remember the scene where she asks [Prince] Albert to marry her, because he was not allowed to ask her. She is the monarch, and had to be the one to ask. That scene was so vulnerable and beautifully twinkly, how Jean-Marc shot that.”

4. “The Adjustment Bureau,” a romantic sci-fi thriller, co-starred Matt Damon. “I remember never being able to get through a scene with Matt Damon without laughing. But I did love the scene in the bathroom where they meet. That scene had to sparkle because otherwise you don’t care about them, and you don’t care about them using their magical fedoras to get back to each other. Matt Damon doesn’t know how to be bad. That’s the truth. He doesn’t know how to play a false note. There is something about what Matt does, and he’s so dexterous in his humanity, but I don’t feel it’s technical with Matt. He’s like a laser beam of truth, and I feel myself, anyone who watches him, they ease back and they go, ‘Oh, thank God, Matt Damon’s here.’ He just leads with the truth. He’s like Josh Brolin. They only know how to be honest, and so they have such humanity to them. That’s why you can’t take your eyes off them. John [Krasinski] and I were so proud of what Matt did [with “The Odyssey”]. It’s obviously the most Herculean undertaking, but he grounded everything with that performance.”

5. “Edge of Tomorrow” (2014, Doug Liman) co-starred Tom Cruise and thrust Blunt into action mode for the first time. Her moment was a war scene set on a beach. “It was the beach set, and we started calling it ‘the bitch’ because it was such a nightmare. That set was always flooded. You were always exposed to terrible elements of the weather, freezing, and we shot that beach scene for a month. Tom Cruise gave me a lot of flowers on that one. He was so good to me, and he revealed halfway through the shoot that this was the deep end of action for him— this was the most challenging action movie that he had ever done, and it was my first action movie, so I was flung in at the deep end of action. But we held each other through that. I loved athletics when I was a kid, and then couldn’t be bothered to work out, and then thought I knew what working out was, and then I realized I didn’t know what working out was until I started training for ‘Edge of Tomorrow,’ and that was a transformational thing to my body. She needed to look lethal, absolutely lethal. And so it helped me a lot, doing all of that physicality.”

6. “Into the Woods” (2014, Rob Marshall), adapted from Stephen Sondheim’s stage musical, boasted a huge ensemble cast; Blunt played the baker’s wife opposite James Corden. “‘Moments in the Woods,’ that big song she has right before she gets squished by the giant. She’s weighing up the duality of life, whether she goes for this poetic interlude in her prosaic life or if she goes back to the prosaic life. That kind of agony that she’s going through in the song was cool. I had I’d never sung in front of anyone before, really, other than one small TV thing years ago. I didn’t even want to audition for it, and Rob Marshall said, ‘Look, I’m not looking for singers who can kind of act. I’m looking for actors who can kind of sing,’ and that was great advice. I said it to my 12-year-old this morning as she went off to her musical audition at school. I said, ‘Don’t worry about the notes; just tell us a story. That’s it. That’s what the song should be, and that’s what will make it sound amazing.'”

7. “Sicario” (2015, Denis Villeneuve) plops Blunt’s straight-arrow FBI agent into a violent Mexican border scenario. “The scene that stands out for me is a spellbinding one, when Benicio del Toro comes to my apartment, and he puts the gun to my face and forces me to sign the contract. It’s right at the end of the movie, and I think that scene holds a special place for me because we were not sure about the scene that was written by Taylor Sheridan. It didn’t feel like it belonged in what we were trying to achieve between the characters. We wanted to change it a little bit. It was an idea that Benicio had. We were racking our brains as to how to finish this scene and this moment between the two characters. He always has so many crazy ideas, and he will have some absolute bangers in there. And he called me at about 11 o’clock the night before, and he goes, ‘I think I have it. What about this?’ And I said, ‘That is a great idea, because you’ve got this very idealistic FBI agent who’s pulled into this incoherent, amoral world. And she’s being forced to sign a contract that says everything they did was aboveboard, and that’s like a death to a character like that.’ We rehearsed that scene for two hours. Denis loved it, and then we all turned to [cinematographer] Roger Deakins: “Roger, what do you think?” And he gave his slow nod of approval, and then we shot it, and it was so.”

8. “A Quiet Place” (2018, John Krasinski) was Blunt’s first experience being directed by her husband. The memorable moment: giving birth in the bathtub as a killer monster hovers nearby, listening for any noise. “We shot that whole sequence from the water breaking in the bathtub in order, which I was grateful to John for. It took four days. We did two takes of that bathtub scene because he shot it mainly as a oner. It starts as the blood’s trickling out, and it comes up, and you see the creature, and then it goes into that scream, and then the fireworks go off, but yeah, it’s a wild scene. It’s really smart to have a baby in a silent world. Every woman I’ve spoken to about that scene, they go: ‘Oh my God, that scene made me cross my legs.” And I was: ‘Okay, all right.'”

9. “Oppenheimer” (2023, Christopher Nolan) offered Blunt a constrained role as Kitty, the recessive wife of the great physicist (Cillian Murphy). Blunt agreed that the scene that earned her the Oscar nomination was in the courtroom where she is badgered by the formidable Jason Clarke. “I knew that was the monster scene. When I read the script, I thought, ‘What an extraordinary scene, that you have this person staggering in, looking like a liability,’ and Chris had written that she almost chokes, and you think she’s going to blow it. When I talked to him about it after I read the script, I said, ‘What a reclamation that scene is of that extraordinary brain coming back to life.’ The brain that had gone crazy at the ironing board, probably meant for bigger things than being someone’s wife and someone’s mummy, and I had a great deal of empathy for her and a lot of women who went crazy at the ironing board. She owns Jason Clarke in a way, and you realize she could probably run circles around him. He played such a wonderful bully in that film, but we saw what Meryl [Streep] did with Miranda Priestley: There’s such power in quiet, great, great power and great dignity.”

10. “The Devil Wears Prada 2” (2026, David Frankel) allowed Blunt to indulge Charlton’s excesses. “We all had scenery stuck in our teeth on that one. It was so fun to go back to playing that lunatic. My favorite scene was the funeral scene where she comes in and rants about Dolce and Gabbana. It was such a ludicrous outfit to be wearing to a funeral. Anne Hathaway is the most unstoppable force. And what a wide range of roles she has access to. I feel this moment in her life. She’s in this full wingspan of being able to harness everything she can do and everything she has to offer, and I can’t believe she had the year she just did, and she was pregnant!”

“Disclosure Day” (2026, Steven Spielberg) leaned on Blunt to carry the sci-fi thriller. “The four-and a-half minute oner in the beginning when she arrives at the news station. I’ve seen what Steven Spielberg can do visually, his visual prowess is rather unparalleled. So to be in a oner that he conjures up on the day, that happened spontaneously — he was planning on covering it. And I said, ‘what would help me so much is if you could let me whirlwind out of control in one take from the moment I pull up, going into the makeup room, coming out speaking Korean, she’s in this incoherent tailspin, and then you see her disintegrate over the course of it. And she gets up there to deliver the weather, and she starts to speak in the alien language. Can we just try it as a oner, just for me to see where I’ve got to get to?’ And he watched me do it. And by the time I got up there to do the weather, my legs were shaking. I was out of breath, beside myself, and he loved it. And he goes, ‘We’re going to do it as a oner.’ And we were done by 2 pm. because he planned to shoot it all day. It was Steven in his element of going, ‘Oh, I see it’ and not only was he intentional about creating the environment for me to be able to do that so he didn’t overcover it, he saw a cinematic advantage.”

Blunt plays several characters in one. “All the stuff in the childhood home was deeply moving because that also dealt with that moment where the character goes from crisis to serenity and the ability to then deploy these powers rather than be puppeteered by them. So I loved that shape-shift in the character, like playing two people throughout the course of this film. And the other moment that felt so human to me was the panic attack in the box car after the train sequence, and she’s at max capacity, bubbling over, overwhelmed, and a few people, including myself on set, had experienced panic attacks, and that felt like a real reaction to someone who was utterly overwhelmed. That also felt so Spielbergian: no one’s a slick elite action hero in Steven’s films. Everyone’s afraid. Everyone, including Indiana Jones, everyone’s scared. That hand that’s shaking on the way to Omaha Beach, that is trauma. He can relate to your vulnerabilities. Everyone’s a bit over their head, and in a different action movie, me and Josh O’Connor would have dropped in the boxcar and gone, ‘Whoa, that was crazy.’ And instead, she has a panic attack. I got them a lot in my early twenties, and Steven’s not immune, neither is Josh. All of us have experienced that. That moment where he takes my hands and he puts them on the piano and he goes, ‘This is real. This is real. Feel this. I’m here. You’re here. We’re here.’ I’ve done that. So it just was like, ‘Oh my God!’ You get to sublimate what you’ve experienced into this creative art form sometimes. That’s the great gift often on movies.”

The languages were right in Blunt’s wheelhouse. She has always loved languages. She learned them two to three months before the start of the shoot. “I learned those scenes. The first thing I learned was the Russian and the Korean, because I wanted it to be spoken at such a velocity that it sounded as conversational as it does as me speaking to you right now, and she doesn’t know she’s speaking Russian,” she said. “She thinks she’s speaking English. You have someone who is white-knuckling their way through most of this film, and these forms of mind control are unconscious to her in the beginning, it’s compulsive.”

Next up: “Walk the Blue Fields” directed by John Crowley and co-starring Andrew Scott as another hot priest, Father Joe, presiding at a wedding. “It’s a short story that I bought the rights to about six years ago by Claire Keegan. If you’ve ever read any of her short stories, they’re like laser beams. They’re so wonderful. My sister Felicity is a book agent. She represents Claire, and she sent it to me. Story A is a wedding day, and story B is what led up to that wedding and why everything is starting to unravel on the wedding day. And it plays like a thriller,” she said. “She’s coming back to Ireland to try to build a relationship with her Irish father [Ciaran Hinds] after they’ve been estranged for years, and it’s a story about identity and religion and love. Andrew Scott has to be one of the most beautiful actors I’ve ever shared a scene with.”

And, of course, John Krasinski’s upcoming “Quiet Place 3,” which co-stars Jack O’Connell, Cillian Murphy, Jason Clarke and Noah Jupe, is shrouded in secrecy. “I don’t want to blow John’s cover here,” she said. And “Sicario 3” is also moving forward with the original cast, a script by James Bond writer Steven Knight and director Padraic McKinley.

#3331. The Best Visual Effects in ‘Wildwood’ Are the Ones You Can’t See — Watch

There are all sorts of magic worlds waiting to be discovered in the stop-motion epic “Wildwood,” but it’s a credit to the film that one of them is Portland, Oregon. Laika Studio’s Head of CG Animation Benoit Dubuc was involved early and often in order to determine what would be shot practically by the stop-motion animation team and what CG effects would be used to achieve. Even in the most mundane and ordinary moments of the film question of either/or. It was one of how the collaboration between different kinds of animation would work.

“We mostly shoot two or three puppets at a time, so any time that there’s background characters, they’re gonna be digital,” Dubuc said during IndieWire’s Craft Roundtable on visual effects. He pointed out that when Baby Mac gets kidnapped by a murder of crows under the command of the dread sorceress Alexandra (Carey Mulligan), the amount of work to achieve that moment fully through stop-motion would mean they’d probably still be animating it. Related Stories From ‘Disclosure Day’ to ‘Devil Wears Prada’: Emily Blunt Breaks Down 10 of Her Greatest Movie Moments How Sound Design Helps ‘Minotaur’ Get Away with Murder

“We’ll often get [animators] to produce some practical work to lead the visual effects work. We built a crow puppet to spec. We didn’t animate it in the film, but it informed the visual effects work. We try to stay away from simulations as much as possible, knowing that what we’re chasing is something that feels handmade and something that is slightly imperfect,” Dubuc said.

That goes for individual characters and for the vibrant backgrounds of “Wildwood” alike. “The audience would think that we built sets the size of an airport hangar with a hundred thousand practical puppets running downhill. It’s not possible,” Dubuc said. The fact that it looks possible, in both the most intricate battle sequences and the ordinary chaos of biking past Powell’s Books, means that the VFX team has done its job. “ The portrayal of Portland that we were striving for is a beautiful, vibrant city,” Dubuc said.

#3330. There's Actually a Simple Explanation for All These Widespread Outages

It feels like every time you look at your phone lately, another company is having an outage. Last week, there was Microsoft, whose outage took down services from Outlook to Teams. Then, the FAA grounded all flights across the U.S. following "communication issues." This week, a number of banks experienced outages, as did Apple. Even the NSA's internal communications network went dark. Some of the biggest corporations and organizations in the world can't seem to keep their services running, leading to widespread disruptions and confusion. When it's a one-off, it's an annoyance; when it's outage after outage, it starts to feel like a pattern.

That pattern, in turn, has begun to fuel anxiety among the general public. What could possibly be causing Apple, Microsoft, JP Morgan Chase, and the NSA alike to go dark at roughly the same time? Is it a coordinated cyberattack? An AI revolt? Is the end finally nigh? To an outside observer, it certainly appears like something coordinated and nefarious is happening here. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is insistent that there is "zero evidence" that hackers or bad actors caused any of these outages, and President Trump is particularly unconcerned by the whole ordeal, saying, "It's life," and "Things like that happen."

But to skeptics of the U.S. government, these trickles of information aren't necessarily reassuring. While I agree with calls for someone from the government (perhaps the president himself) to make an official announcement explaining the situation, the root cause does appear to be clear at this time: The short answer? AI is at fault here, but not in the way you think.

Love it or hate it, AI is a force to be reckoned with. While you might know that AI can generate hyper-realistic videos and manage your emails on your behalf, certain models are adept at discovering new security vulnerabilities in software. These models aren't just helpful tools; they far surpass the abilities of human researchers. You might remember Anthropic initially pulled the brakes on its breakthrough model, Claude Mythos, when it found that the model could root out security vulnerabilities in just about anything.

Mythos, and models like it, are a double-edged sword. On the one hand, they can be major assets for developers and researchers to find new security vulnerabilities that humans otherwise wouldn't have discovered, and patch them accordingly. Unfortunately, the same can be said for bad actors, who can use these models to learn about new security flaws and attempt to exploit them before researchers have a chance to find them. As such, software developers across the spectrum, from small-time devs to major corporations, have been racing to patch as many security vulnerabilities as they can find—and they're finding a lot.

You might notice your PC's security updates, for example, are shipping with more patches than usual—historic levels, even. Microsoft keeps breaking its own records with its Patch Tuesday updates, including over 1,400 fixes with its October update. The company's October 2025 Patch Tuesday update, by comparison, included fewer than 180 fixes.

It's important to understand that just about every company that develops software is furiously working to patch its systems before hackers or AI agents exploit vulnerabilities first. And while there are successes (Microsoft is now protecting its customers from thousands of flaws each month), this speed is also inadvertently breaking things along the way. That's not just speculation: According to The Washington Sun, both Wall Street executives and the NSA explained to members of Congress that patching security flaws discovered by AI models caused this week's widespread outages.

Barring some campaign to cover up a coordinated attack on systems and services, it does seem like these outages are simply the result of companies breaking their own products in an attempt to stop AI-assisted hackers from exploiting undiscovered flaws. But that's not all that reassuring, either. AI models are only going to keep getting better at finding vulnerabilities; likewise, AI agents are only improving at hacking into systems autonomously. Companies will need to ramp up their efforts to patch their software before both hackers and AI agents discover those flaws first, and so the cycle will continue. Unless something changes, we may see routine outages as companies try to fix things as quickly as possible.

The implications aren't specific to any one company, either. Our world increasingly relies on fewer companies to keep us all connected. We saw that last year, when cloud hosting providers like AWS and Cloudflare each experienced outages. When these services go down, so do all of the networks that rely on them. If AWS or Cloudflare break something while trying to patch their systems, whole parts of the internet go dark.

Of course, it'll only be more difficult for the general public—if not the developers themselves—to recognize when outages are the result of maintenance or a cyberattack. Just because recent outages don't appear to be nefarious in nature, that doesn't mean future outages will be so innocent. For the time being, however, it seems we can worry less about an active cybersecurity incident, and more about how AI is disrupting modern life in ways few of us saw coming.

#3328. Darkseid Unveils His Justice League, All Members And Powers

The Justice League are DC's greatest heroes - bastions of heroism and self-sacrifice - which makes it all the more disturbing that Darkseid just assembled his own version of the team. His roster combines some shock members with heavyweights designed to counter Batman, Superman and Wonder Woman.

Recent years have seen Darkseid take his rightful place as the overarching villain of all DC canon, as 2024's All In Special saw him leave behind his mortal limits and become a multiversal god, founding the Absolute Universe and spreading his influence out into the multiverse.

The recent DC All In Saga: Darkseid vs. the World #1 (Scott Snyder, Sanford Greene) confirmed that his plans remain on track, as well as revealing that the God of Evil has assembled his own personal Justice League. Here's every member of Darkseid's superhuman army (at least, so far.)

DC All In Saga: Darkseid vs. the World #1 sees Darkseid arrive on Earth-3, the home of the villainous Crime Syndicate. This group is DC's classic evil Justice League, mirroring the heroes of classic canon. Darkseid demands the Syndicate join him as his thralls, only for their leader Ultraman to launch an attack on Darkseid. Of course, he's quickly beaten to a pulp and drafted into the archvillain's service.

An incredibly powerful bully, Ultraman keeps Earth-3 under his thumb despite not being particularly intelligent or creative with his powers. He has the basic abilities of Superman, with the exception that Kryptonite only makes him stronger, leading him to seek out, crush and snort the radioactive rock wherever he finds it.

Ultraman once imprisoned Superman's son in his dimension, taunting and abusing him for years, leading the mainstream Clark Kent to develop a seething hatred of his opposite number. Recently, DC introduced Ultraman and Superwoman's son Ultraboy, though he isn't shown on Earth-3 when Darkseid attacks the Syndicate.

Having arranged the assassination of his mother and father as a child, Owlman used their fortune to take total control of Gotham city, turning it into his personal kingdom. A genius tactician and combatant, Owlman has an army of 'Talon' sidekicks who he considers totally disposable, sacrificing them on a whim.

Owlman chafes under Ultraman's absolute power, engaging in a stunted affair with Superwoman behind his back. Owlman is one of the few denizens of Earth-3 whose counterpart in DC's main continuity is also a villain - a rival to the Court of Owls formerly known as Lincoln March but claiming to be Batman's brother.

Earth-3's Superwoman is essentially a superpowered dominatrix. She's married to Ultraman but carries out a series of affairs to secretly influence the planet's politics, its supervillain rulers and even its heroes.

Despite being an Amazon, Superwoman possesses the power of the mainstream Superman, with the exception of wielding the Lasso of Submission - a length of barbed wire which forces whoever it binds to worship and obey its wielder.

Possessing the powers of the Flash, Johnny Quick is a superspeed serial killer who takes joy in running through normal humans, causing them to explode. Unlike the mainstream Flash, he's not particularly intelligent, and tends to follow the lead of Crime Syndicate member Atomica, who isn't shown as a member of the Syndicate in DC All In Saga: Darkseid vs. the World #1.

There have been multiple versions of the evil Green Lantern in DC lore, and it's unclear which one appears in DC All In Saga: Darkseid vs. the World #1. The most recent was John Stewart's Emerald Knight. A former police officer, Stewart was recruited by the Overlords of Oa as one of their personal enforcers.

As the Emerald Knight, John can summon powerful energy constructs, with his ring persuading him to kill at every opportunity. His vigilante murders estranged him from his daughter, leading to a further surrender of his humanity to the ring.

In contrast, the former Power Ring of Earth-3 wore a ring powered by the demonic Volthoom, which essentially enslaved the wearer and fed on their lifeforce, unleashing monstrous energy constructs when a fight was to its benefit.

The character shown in Darkseid's Justice League is John Stewart but is referred to as Power Ring, raising questions about which version is considered canon in this frequently rebooted reality.

A mysterious figure straight out of Greek mythology, Pandora is a skilled mystic with a range of magical abilities. Despite powerful magic, she prefers to fight by channeling her power through twin handguns, and is a master of modern and traditional weaponry.

Dying at the hands of Doctor Manhattan at the beginning of DC's Rebirth era, Pandora has been resurrected as Darkseid's "harbinger." He has tasked her with traveling across the multiverse, offering his most powerful enemies the chance to join him. Her first stop is the corpse of the beyond-godlike villain Imperiex, who it's suggested she intends to bring back to life.

Pandora believes that Darkseid intends to eventually consume her (and the villains she recruits) to obtain the 'Omega energy' that is powering his ultimate form, but is content to go along with his plans for the present.

The recent Superman Annual 2026: Year One Thousand revealed that Darkseid has embarked on an agreement with Brainiac, working together to limit Superman's power and influence across the multiverse. Brainiac has taken on the task of kidnapping every version of the Legion of Super-Heroes from across every reality.

Brainiac is at the height of his power, with a gigantic body and godlike technology that makes him a multiversal force. Indeed, he's so powerful that Cyborg Superman (aka Hank Henshaw) is acting as his enforcer, with Brainiac tasking him to patrol the future and ensure no new Legion of Super-Heroes ever forms.

Cyborg Superman has all Clark Kent's powers, plus the ability to take control of essentially all forms of machinery. It appears that the pair may soon split off on their own, with Brainiac scheming to use the combined power of the various Legions he's captured to topple both Darkseid AND Superman. For now, however, he remains in Darkseid's alliance.

The awesome conclusion of DC All In Saga: Darkseid vs. the World #1 reveals the full scale of Darkseid's Justice League. While he spends the issue pacifying and capturing the Crime Syndicate, he then reveals that "I have conquered nearly all variants of Earth" across the multiverse.

He ends the issue surrounded by versions of Superman he's captured and stored in tanks, presumably with the same offer he gives the Crime Syndicate - join him or be consumed as a power source.

While it's not known exactly which versions of Superman Darkseid has control over, it's likely the following 'evil Superman' are among his soldiers:

With the Crime Syndicate, the scheming Pandora and an endless army of Supermen, Darkseid has assembled the ultimate evil Justice League, leaving fans to ask how the heroes of DC's main reality can ever stand a chance against what's coming.

#3327. AI Film ‘Gods Don’t Give Gifts’ Deemed Ineligible by Academy for Best Animated Feature Oscar

“Gods Don’t Give Gifts,” an upcoming film from YouTuber Gossip Goblin that was made entirely with generated artificial intelligence, was deemed ineligible for the Best Animated Feature Oscar at the upcoming Academy Awards.

As IndieWire previously reported on “Gods Don’t Give Gifts,” which is the first fully AI movie to be released theatrically, the film had submitted for consideration and had planned FYC screenings alongside its theatrical release on December 4.

But the film was not included among the list of 38 animated films deemed eligible for this year’s Oscars that were announced Monday, November 23. IndieWire understands that the Academy’s Animation Branch Executive Committee determined “Gods Don’t Give Gifts” did not meet the Academy’s definition of an animated film under the rules for the 99th Awards. Related Stories The Best Visual Effects in ‘Wildwood’ Are the Ones You Can’t See — Watch From ‘Disclosure Day’ to ‘Devil Wears Prada’: Emily Blunt Breaks Down 10 of Her Greatest Movie Moments

Here’s the full rule as written that the Academy felt “Gods Don’t Give Gifts” did not satisfy:

An animated film is one in which characters or objects are given the illusion of life by having movement created for them, by any human means. While the crucial movement of a live-action motion picture is captured at speed, animation is the craft of human creation and manipulation of images to produce a performance from inanimate objects. At least 75 percent of the motion picture’s running time, without opening or end credits, must include animation of the primary subject or subjects. An animated feature has a running time of more than 40 minutes. Upon submission, filmmakers must provide information supporting how the motion picture qualifies as an animated film.

Edward Saatchi, a producer on “Gods Don’t Give Gifts” with Fable Studios, told IndieWire he and director Zack London (a.k.a. Gossip Goblin) plan to appeal the animation branch’s decision and cited the example of Richard Linklater’s rotoscoped film “Apollo 10 1/2,” which was originally deemed ineligible but saw the branch reverse its decision upon appeal. Saatchi said that the film, in addition to submitting for Best Animated Feature, also submitted in other categories such as Best Director, Adapted Screenplay, VFX, and Sound. But if the film doesn’t fall under the animation branch today, he believes eventually AI movies will inevitably find a place somewhere within Academy rules, even if it ends up being a theoretical “Best AI Movie” category.

“‘Gods Don’t Give Gifts’ is starting a big debate around where cinematic works of art made with AI fit. Is it time to consider a ‘Best AI Movie?’ Do these films fit best in the voice-actor led animation category? Is AI simply the new VFX? It’s going to take the whole industry time to figure it out,” Saatchi said. “With traditional garlanded directors like Matthieu Kassovitz, Alex Proyas, and Doug Liman making heavily-AI films, it’s going to be a good debate of how to categorize. We think Best Animated is simplest, but it may be the Academy decides ultimately that a Best AI movie category will make the most sense with these films where everything you’re seeing is generative.”

Of note, one of the films that did qualify for Best Animated Feature was “Coyote vs. Acme,” which is a hybrid animated and live-action film featuring the Looney Tunes alongside human actors in the real world. The Academy on Monday also announced the eligible features in the Best Documentary Feature race and the Best International Feature race.

As part of the Academy’s most recent rules changes from earlier this year, only roles credited in the film’s legal billing that are demonstrably performed by humans with their consent are eligible for acting categories, and screenplays must be human-authored to be eligible. That rule changed followed on guidelines from last year ahead of the 98th Oscars in which the Academy specified, “[Gen-AI] tools neither help nor harm the chances of achieving a nomination. The Academy and each branch will judge the achievement, taking into account the degree to which a human was at the heart of the creative authorship when choosing which movie to award.”

In the case of “Gods Don’t Give Gifts,” the film has a script written by London, and though all the characters in the film are generated with AI visually, it features real human actors doing the voice work for the characters. The film also features cameos of some real-life people playing parts resembling themselves, most notably the pop star Grimes. But the film has elaborate look books, visual reference points, and photo mashing that all went into the creation of these characters, something that clearly has human authorship and goes beyond a computer interpreting a single prompt.

Part of Gossip Goblin’s battle in legitimizing “Gods Don’t Give Gifts” is in showing there was a human team, between 30-35 people, working for years on the film’s creation. Gossip Goblin also recently released a behind-the-scenes documentary that showcases the film’s composer, its foley artist, its voice actors, and more detailing the human effort that went into the project.

Discussion over AI in Oscar eligible films came to a head after several movies in the 2024 Oscar race were reported to have included AI in their post-production editing process, including “A Complete Unknown,” “The Brutalist,” and “Emilia Pérez.” The examples were for traditional VFX, not for anything that enhanced or altered performances, but the Academy as a result now requires disclosure of AI if it is used in a film.

“Gods Don’t Give Gifts” begins its theatrical run on December 4, which will initially be an Oscar-qualifying run, and it will expand on January 22 alongside a rollout with the film’s international distributor AGC International.

#3325. Why Is the ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Trailer So… Gloomy? Internet Erupts Over Latest Look at Marvel Movie

There’s a storm brewing, chere, and it has nothing to do with the weird Gambit (Channing Tatum) and Herbie the Robot Dunkin Donuts ads that played like once a quarter during all the football games on Sunday.

The final trailer was released ahead of Marvel’s “Avengers: Doomsday,” the mega-Sentinel, crossover-tastic 165-minute Russo Brothers opus out on December 18. And the response hasn’t been great — in part because Cyclops says, “To me, my X-Men!” and there isn’t actually a Storm.

Way back in the salad days of 2012, Joss Whedon first did an “Assemble” shot that roved in a circle all of the original “Avengers” film, while an Alan Silvestri score bwaaamped the brassy “Avengers” theme. Say whatever you like about Whedon’s strengths and weaknesses when it comes to visual style, but the first time this happened, the shot’s continuous nature served a storytelling purpose. It was the cinematic way to finally bind these crazy kids together in superhero fellowship — through the timeless crucible of New York City getting shredded into CGI bits by alien-monster things. Related Stories AI Film ‘Gods Don’t Give Gifts’ Deemed Ineligible by Academy for Best Animated Feature Oscar The Best Visual Effects in ‘Wildwood’ Are the Ones You Can’t See — Watch

But over the many, many Phases of the MCU, the Avengers Assemble shots have kept happening. And happening. And sure enough, the “Doomsday” trailer crescendos with a bunch of our heroes stuck in a gray-black wasteland void that looks like a glitched “Expedition 33” loading screen, with the camera straining to create that same sense of unity.

It doesn’t. At least not in the trailer. Which is why so much of the response to the finale “Doomsday” trailer has been focused on it.

As folks online have pointed out, Steve Rogers (Chris Evans) looks like he’s standing in entirely different lighting from the people closest to him. There’s no sense of texture or proximity that suggests anybody was placed against the same green screen together, let alone acting together (a problem that has been pointed out about the filmmaking process for “Doomsday” already).

No amount of money can make up for shooting for maximum flexibility — which so often can devolve into being indecisive — or for pursuing relentless revisions throughout the VFX pipeline. That is exactly what leads to shadowy, sloppily-framed environments like wherever the hell the Avengers are fighting Doctor Doom (Robert Downey Jr.) and his creations. And because the environment is so flattened and indistinct, only the barest hints of color survive. And really, only because Reed Richards (Pedro Pascal) is still wearing a coat from a different movie.

Now, what comes most naturally to Cyclops is shooting an optic blast from his eyes, and what comes most naturally to us is posting negative takes online. The trailer takes that shot out of context for nostalgia’s sake; its dramatic purpose within the film itself might be more complicated, or the setup for a twist in three different timelines’ worth of Avengers’ fortunes. But when it comes to all the cinematic crimes of artless visuals, repetitive plots, and overbearing lore that have contributed to superhero fatigue? The “Avengers: Doomsday” trailer doesn’t seem to be beating the charges.

Shealyn Scott is a Senior Writer at Screen Rant. She has been writing for the site since 2024, focused on network, reality, streaming, and classic television. One of the best K-dramas of the year is deservedly climbing the charts on Disney+ and Hulu. Based on the 2018 web novel and later webtoon of the same name, The Remarried Empress follows titular Empress Navier (Shin Min-a), who is forced into a corner after her husband, Emperor Sovieshu (Ju Ji-hoon), throws away their marriage. The record-breaking premiere of The Remarried Empress started the series off with a bang, and the eight-episode K-drama has continually been a top performer for Disney+/Hulu since. In fact, the only title consistently outperforming it is Percy Jackson and the Olympians (via Flix Patrol).

Beyond having a built-in fandom from the hit source material, The Remarried Empress immediately attracted attention with its star-studded cast. Shin Min-a is easily one of the most renowned K-drama actresses in modern history, but pairing her with familiar heartthrob Lee Jong-suk (Heinrey) has been a true delight. Of course, there's more than enough to enjoy for viewers who aren't well-versed in the K-drama industry. Even if the basic premise doesn't instantly appeal, watching a single episode will reveal the true selling point of The Remarried Empress: a stunning, slow-burn fantasy romance that is meticulously crafted for every prospective viewer.

Despite the summary detailing major plot points like Sovieshu and Navier divorcing— and a strategic partnership with Heinrey making the latter the eponymous "remarried empress" in the first place— the Disney+ K-drama has taken an unconventional approach to adapting the illustrious webtoon. The bulk of the first season has been spent establishing its main characters and showing the audience the deterioration of Navier and Sovieshu's relationship in brutal clarity. Rather than breeze through the beginning and have Sovieshu leave the main character for Rashta (Lee Se-young) by the pilot episode's end, The Remarried Empress centers the familiar story on Navier.

Without question, each member of the extensive ensemble plays an important role in the overarching plot, but the titular character is the centerpiece of every dramatic revelation, shocking twist, and emotional decision that threatens to upend the entire empire. As the gripping narrative grows taut and tense, the stunning aesthetics of the show soften the blow, with sprawling landscapes and ornate interior shots building a beguiling setting while gorgeous costumes complement each character in their own unique color palette. Undoubtedly, the K-drama's every detail is utterly transporting, making it impossible for viewers not to fully immerse themselves in the story.

To that end, there's also incredible balance within the writing. The Remarried Empress refuses to give the audience perfect information, instead choosing deliberate moments to introduce pivotal characters, unveil transformative lore, and reveal just enough disruptive information to make the viewer question everything they know about a given subject. Consequently, The Remarried Empress wields the political drama and turmoil of a historical K-drama whilst it slowly but surely composes a love story that feels fantastic in every sense of the word. Irrefutably, the series is one of the biggest successes of the year— and it couldn't have come soon enough.

Nearly every major streaming service has invested in the production of original Korean content throughout the past decade, but Netflix K-dramas have overwhelmingly been the most popular. Be it dramas that went straight into the pop culture zeitgeist like Squid Game or multi-season favorites like All of Us Are Dead and The Trauma Code: Heroes on Call, Netflix is steadily creating K-dramas that eclipse almost anything comparable released on competing platforms. Obviously, Disney+ and Hulu have had their own successes, but titles like Moving, Made in Korea, and Perfect Crown simply don't have the same reach.

From harrowing depictions of real-life monarchies to modern twists on classic Cinderella stories, these K-dramas promise a royally good time.

As such, distributing something like The Remarried Empress— a long-awaited adaptation of a massive webtoon with a staggering cast to boot— is precisely what Disney +/Hulu needed to stay in the K-drama game. Admittedly, Netflix has dropped its fair share of amazing contributions this year, but very few can match the sheer scope of The Remarried Empress. Should the fantasy romance land a well-earned second season, Disney+ will have a multipart sensation on its hands soon enough. Yet, even if the drama isn't renewed, its eight-episode run is a worthy binge-watch that genre fans will fall head over heels for.

The Church of Scientology is coming after Leah Remini ... and this time, it's hitting the former "King of Queens" star where it hurts -- her wallet.

While the courts have thrown out numerous allegations, her lawsuit has not been dismissed entirely ... and some claims are still moving forward.

The Church is seeking the money under California's anti-SLAPP law, which allows successful defendants to recover certain legal fees in cases involving protected speech.

A hearing on the fee request is scheduled for January ... but for now, Scientology is claiming victory ... and asking Remini to pick up a very expensive tab.

#3314. Guy Ritchie’s 126-Minute Fantasy Epic Officially Earns 179 Million Views on Netflix

Guy Ritchie is turning into Taylor Sheridan these days with the amount of television series he's got his hand in right now. He's enjoying plenty of success on streaming at the moment with the likes of MobLand, The Gentlemen, and Young Sherlock, but some of his older movies have also found an audience that wasn't necessarily there when they were released in theaters as a result of Ritchie's big wins on the small screen. A decade ago, Ritchie decided to try his hand at a $175 million fantasy epic that Warner Bros. had hoped would launch an entire franchise, but those plans were abandoned when the movie failed to make back its production budget at the box office. Nine years later, though, it's becoming one of those Netflix sleeper hits.

Ritchie's King Arthur: Legend of the Sword has officially recorded 179 million minutes viewed on Netflix, placing eighth on Nielsen's movie streaming chart in the United States for the week of November 2–8. Given the movie's 126-minute runtime, that's the equivalent of approximately 1.42 million complete viewings in a single week.

The film is an iconoclastic take on the classic Excalibur myth, tracing Arthur's journey from the streets to the throne. When the child Arthur's father is murdered, Vortigern, Arthur's uncle, seizes the crown. Robbed of his birthright and with no idea who he truly is, Arthur comes up the hard way in the back alleys of the city. But once he pulls the sword from the stone, his life is turned upside down and he is forced to acknowledge his true legacy — whether he likes it or not.

King Arthur: Legend of the Sword grossed just $149.2 million worldwide against its $175 million production budget, which obviously isn't the result anybody was hoping for. Critically, it didn't fare much better either, sitting on a 31% critics' score on Rotten Tomatoes. However, at least the audience kinda liked it, as it has a considerably healthier 69% audience score. Nice.

The cast includes Charlie Hunnam (Sons of Anarchy) as Arthur, Jude Law (The Holiday) as Vortigern, Àstrid Bergès-Frisbey (Pirates of the Caribbean: On Stranger Tides) as the Mage, Djimon Hounsou (Gladiator) as Bedivere, Eric Bana (Troy) as Uther Pendragon, Aidan Gillen (Game of Thrones) as Bill, Freddie Fox (House of the Dragon) as Rubio, and Annabelle Wallis (Peaky Blinders) as Maggie.

King Arthur: Legend of the Sword is streaming now on Netflix in the United States. Stay tuned to Collider for all the latest news and updates on the biggest and best movies and shows heading to your favorite streaming platforms soon.

#3312. Paralympic Wheelchair Basketball Silver Medalist Lee Fryer Charged with Rape

Lee Fryer -- a wheelchair basketball player who won a silver medal at the 2024 Paralympics with Great Britain -- has been charged with rape in the United Kingdom.

According to multiple reports ... Fryer is facing 17 charges, including 11 counts of rape for alleged incidents prosecutors say took place between May 2021 and May 2026.

The first alleged rape is said to have taken place in 2021 when Fryer was 18 years old.

Fryer's criminal charges also include the alleged oral, vaginal and anal rapes of a woman in Spain between September 2023 and March 2024.

He's also facing sexual assault charges from alleged incidents in South Africa ... and charges of voyeurism, intentional strangulation, assault and controlling or coercive behaviour in an intimate relationship.

Fryer played for the Great Britain Paralympic team in 2024, which narrowly lost the gold medal to the USA in a 73-69 nail-biter.

His trial is scheduled for March. If convicted on all counts, he could receive a life sentence.

LeBron James may be the King, but his castle apparently has a trespassing problem ... and his wife Savannah James wants a judge to help guard the gates.

According to court documents, obtained by TMZ, Savannah has filed two separate requests for temporary restraining orders against William Rahman and Jaliere McWhite ... accusing both men of repeatedly showing up uninvited at the family's Los Angeles properties.

And one of them apparently came ready to move in ... Savannah claims Rahman arrived at her property in an Uber on November 14 with several pieces of luggage ... refusing to leave despite repeated warnings from security.

Police eventually responded, but Rahman allegedly insisted the house was his and threatened legal action to have security removed.

According to the filing, Rahman had been sending mail and packages to the family's address since December 2025 ... prompting Savannah's attorneys to send him a cease-and-desist letter in February.

Meanwhile, McWhite is the man TMZ previously reported was arrested after allegedly showing up at LeBron's home claiming to be his son.

Savannah's filing paints an even scarier picture ... alleging McWhite actually entered one of the family's homes on November 6, shortly after relatives left the front door unlocked.

She also claims McWhite showed up at another family property in October, when police placed him on a mental health hold.

Savannah is seeking protection for herself, LeBron, and their 3 children ... though the court's rulings on the restraining order requests were not yet available.

#3307. 3 Best Prime Video Movies To Watch This Week (Nov 23-27)

The number one movie on Prime Video this week is David O. Russell’s Madden. Starring Nicolas Cage as the iconic NFL coach and commentator, the sports biopic explores John Madden’s colorful life and career, with Christian Bale, Kathryn Hahn, John Mulaney, and more in supporting roles. Though critically panned, the movie has received a lot of attention since its arrival on the platform last week, but it’s hardly the only thing worth seeing on the streaming service. Here’s a look at three great movies that we think you should watch on Prime Video this week.

For more recommendations, check out our list of the best shows and movies on Prime Video.

A quintessential coming-of-age film of the 21st century, The Perks of Being a Wallflower is Stephen Chbosky’s film adaptation of his 1999 novel, following Charlie, a teenager who shares his experiences from his freshman year of high school in a series of letters. The film follows his trials and triumphs as an adolescent who also suffers from severe trauma, which he remains largely unaware of. Logan Lerman plays Charlie, with Emma Watson and Ezra Miller as his closest friends.

Heartfelt and sincere, The Perks of Being a Wallflower is considered among the most mature of teen films. Chbosky compellingly translates the charm of his modern YA classic onto the screen, with award-winning performances by its leading trio infusing life into the beloved characters. The film has since become a cult hit and remains a defining element of 2010s pop culture.

Every one of these four started as a cast recording people played until the disc wore out, and every one of them eventually turned into a film. Here is yours, what it says about you, and the case for it being the best of the four.

You work like the clock is against you, because in your head it always is. Hamilton is three hours about a man who cannot stop producing, cannot stop arguing and cannot leave a single thing alone, and you recognised yourself in it immediately.

People made up their minds about you early and they were wrong. Wicked takes the most famous villain in American children's fiction and asks what the story looks like from her side, which is a question you have asked about yourself more than once.

You cannot walk past something unfair. Les Mis is a show about a man who spends his entire life trying to make one wrong right, and about everybody around him deciding what they are prepared to lose for other people.

You are not interested in saving it all for later. Rent is a year in the life of people with no money, no plan and a very clear sense that the time they have is the only thing they genuinely own.

In her second feature directorial, Maggie Gyllenhaal reimagines the 1935 film by James Whale, which was inspired by Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus. Set in 1930s Chicago, The Bride follows Frankenstein’s monster, aka Frank, as he enlists the help of a revolutionary medical genius named Dr. Euphronius (Annette Bening) to give him a companion and discovers that his new bride has a past and future beyond his control. Jessie Buckley stars as the titular counterpart to Christian Bale's Frank, with Peter Sarsgaard, Jake Gyllenhaal, and Penélope Cruz as other important characters.

The Bride is not just a modernist look at the 19th-century novel but a feminist revision of a Hollywood classic that thrives primarily on Jessie Buckley’s electrifying, if chaotic, performance. The film received massively polarized reviews but earned universal praise for the lead performances, set design, and costumes. Criticisms aside, the film does add a new perspective to a classic legend: a dark Bonnie-and-Clyde-style mid-century Gothic drama.

Directed and choreographed by Adam Shankman and written by Leslie Dixon, 2007’s Hairspray is a film adaptation of the 2002 musical by Mark O'Donnell and Thomas Meehan, which in turn is a stage adaptation of the 1998 film of the same name. Set in 1962 Baltimore, Maryland, the romantic comedy musical follows the pursuits of a “pleasantly plump” teenager named Tracy (Nikki Blonsky) who strives to become a dancing star on a local TV show and rallies against racial segregation. The film also boasts a stellar ensemble featuring John Travolta, Michelle Pfeiffer, and Christopher Walken, among others.

Adam Shankman turned a cult classic into a mainstream genre hit of its time, making Hairspray a worldwide critical and commercial success. Energetic and fun, with foot-tapping musical numbers, the film is a well-rounded entertainer that successfully retains the spirit of the original while also being refreshingly new. John Travolta’s drag performance in the movie may have drawn mixed reactions, but Hairspray easily ranks among the best musicals of the 21st century.

#3303. Six Things You Should Do Now to Optimize Your Setup for GTA 6

You’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI. You’ve preloaded the game on your console, you’ve taken the next month off work, and you’ve locked your phone in a Faraday cage and set it adrift at sea. You’re prepared to lock in, and you haven’t forgotten a thing…right? Well, just to make sure, here are the most important tips to optimize your setup before you fire up the most anticipated game of the decade.

GTA 6 is absurdly large. According to Rockstar, you’ll need up to 212GB of storage space. For high-end consoles like the PS5 Pro, that’s more than 10% of the available storage space, and close to half the space on the more budget-conscious Xbox Series S. There’s a good chance you’ll have to delete something to make room.

Alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it). External SSDs are probably the cheapest route, though you’ll want to make sure to use a high-speed USB cable to connect it. It’s even worth shopping around for alternate models of SSD. For example, at the time of writing, the popular 2TB WD_BLACK external drive was close to $200, but the exact same drive in pink was $132.

You can also directly upgrade the storage of your console with expansion drives. The Xbox Series X|S supports proprietary expansion cards, while the PS5 and PS5 Pro can accept most M.2 internal SSDs. These will generally be faster, since they plug directly into the console via higher-speed connections than a drive hooked up via USB.

Let’s face it: Half the fun of any sandbox game is the weird, unique stuff that happens to only you. So you’re probably going to be hitting that “record recent gameplay” button more often than usual. While you’re cleaning up your storage space (or adding more), make sure to account for all the video clips you might want to save.

File size of video clips depends on a lot of factors, but 4K recordings can generally take up to 0.5GB per minute of footage. You can cut that down by saving footage in 1080p instead, but either way you’ll want to leave a little extra space.

Game footage is also a pretty good place to look if you need to make room on your console and don’t want to delete any games. Be honest with yourself: You don’t need all those clips from Horizon Forbidden West you saved four years ago. Dive into the settings on your console and find the biggest media files you forgot you even had on there.

According to Rockstar, GTA 6 will be targeting 30fps across consoles at launch, which is pretty low as modern AAA games go. Part of the reason for that is all the processing power going to rendering a complex environment, but it also means you won’t need a fancy high frame rate TV or monitor any time soon to get the most out of it. Still, it couldn’t hurt to check a few settings on your display.

First, make sure you’re using a higher refresh rate than 30Hz. While the game is targeting 30fps, it is technically capable of more, so if your console can keep up, you don’t want to accidentally bottleneck your frames. This setting will vary by device, so check the manual that came with your screen.

Also, make sure you have HDR enabled on your hardware. There’s a good chance this is already turned on for your TV, but sometimes other devices can switch display modes if they only support SDR. The game will help you calibrate your HDR settings for GTA 6 specifically when you launch it, but only if it detects HDR compatibility in the first place.

If you’re planning to buy a console specifically for GTA 6, this might be one of those rare instances where a PS5 Pro really is worth the upgrade. According to Rockstar, certain features like ray-traced shadows will only be available on the Pro version of Sony’s console.

More importantly, the PS5 Pro version supports PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (or PSSR), which upscales lower-resolution images to get better detail and higher frame rates out of the same hardware. Given that GTA 6 is already starting at a meager target of 30fps on most consoles, anything that can give your frame rate a boost is probably going to feel like a welcome improvement over the baseline.

I’ll tell you a secret as someone who’s spent a lot of time testing different game controllers: Most of the time, you really don’t need an expensive “elite” controller. Most of the time. I don’t buy into the idea that a taller control stick is going to make you an esports athlete. It can be nice to have, but it’s not a game changer. What does matter is customizing your controls, especially for long gaming sessions.

The DualSense Edge wireless controller is a favorite of mine, mainly because of the rear paddles and adjustable triggers. The former lets you map any button to a rear lever that you can access with your fingers underneath the controller, which can often ease some of the wrist strain of awkward button combos. And the adjustable triggers let you activate the buttons with less motion, again reducing repetitive stress.

The Xbox Elite Series 2 controller has similar features for the Xbox, as well as custom caps for the D-pad. Both consoles’ versions of pro controllers are more expensive than the standard ones, but if you’re planning to game for many hours, it can be worth it to get a controller that’s more comfortable for you.

If you have an Xbox One, you don’t necessarily have to upgrade your console to play GTA 6, but you might want to take a look at your network. GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on day one, and you’ll be able to stream the game to an Xbox One console (as long as you purchase Cloud playtime as well or get some with your Game Pass subscription). This is the only way to play on a console older than the current generation, so if you don’t want to shell out for new hardware, this might be your best bet.

Xbox recommends a minimum of a 20Mbps connection to run cloud gaming, but more is obviously better. If you can connect your console to a wired Ethernet connection, that would be better and provide more stability. If you can’t connect a cable, then at least make sure you’re well within range of your wifi router, and try to limit any other bandwidth-hogging applications on the network while you’re playing.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If you've been hearing a lot about Claude Code lately but assumed it was only for software developers, you're missing out on one of the most powerful ways to use AI right now.

Anthropic's coding agent can build websites, create personalized apps, automate repetitive tasks and develop tools that would otherwise require hours of programming experience. And thanks to the Claude desktop app, you don't even need to know how to use a terminal.

Unlike a traditional AI chatbot that gives you instructions for building something, Claude Code can do much of the work itself. You describe what you want in plain English, which is also known as "vibe coding," and Claude can create the necessary files, write the code, test its work and make adjustments based on your feedback.

Here's everything you need to know to get started, including five beginner-friendly projects worth trying.

Claude Code is Anthropic's AI coding agent. Although it was originally designed for software developers, it's also useful for anyone who wants to build their own digital tools.

Say you've been searching for a budgeting app but can't find one that does exactly what you want. Instead of downloading another app or paying for another subscription, you could ask Claude Code to build one tailored to your needs.

The biggest difference between Claude Code and a regular Claude conversation is that Claude Code can work directly with files on your computer, run commands and make changes to a project with your permission.

Sign up to the Tom's AI Guide weekly newsletter summing up all the biggest AI news you need to know. Plus, analysis from our AI editors and tips on how to use the latest AI tools!

You don't need to copy and paste hundreds of lines of code or figure out where to put them.

Claude Code isn't included in Anthropic's free subscription, so you'll need a paid plan to access it, with Claude Pro starting at $20 per month.

There are two main ways to get started on your computer.

Option 1: Use the Claude desktop app (recommended)

This is the easiest route for beginners because you won't have to install any additional coding software. Visit claude.com/download.

Download the app for your operating system. Install the app and sign in to your Claude account. Select the Code tab. Start a new local session and select a folder for your project. I'd recommend creating an empty folder called "My First Claude App" on your computer before getting started.

Option 2: Install Claude Code in your terminal

If you're comfortable using command-line tools, you can install Claude Code directly. On Mac or Linux, open your terminal and enter:

curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash

Once installed, enter claude and follow the instructions to authenticate your account. Anthropic also offers Claude Code through the web, where projects can run on the company's cloud infrastructure.

For your first project, I'd recommend building something small that you can actually use. A personalized daily planner is a great place to start because it doesn't require external services or complicated software.

Select your project folder and enter the following prompt:

Build me a personal daily planner that runs in my web browser. Include a to-do list, three daily priorities, a habit tracker and a notes section. Give it a clean, modern design and automatically save my progress locally. Use plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript without external dependencies. Explain how to open the finished app.

Claude should begin working on your project, creating the files necessary to make it function.

Once it's finished, ask Claude to open or preview the app. You can continue refining your creation with conversational instructions such as "Add dark mode," "Make the text bigger" or "Add a button to reset my daily tasks."

You don't have to get your initial prompt perfect. Building with Claude Code is an ongoing conversation, and some of the best features might come from ideas you have after seeing the first version.

You can create a dashboard that tracks expenses, calculates monthly savings and displays spending by category and even tailor it to your household instead of adapting to someone else's budgeting system. Try the prompt: Build me a personalized household budget tracker that runs in my web browser. Include monthly income, recurring bills, everyday expenses and savings goals. Automatically calculate how much money I have left each month and display spending by category using interactive charts. Let me add, edit and delete expenses, customize spending categories and track my progress toward savings goals. Give it a clean, modern design and save my data locally so it stays private. Explain how to open and use the finished app.

Build a personal portfolio, small-business website or blog. Describe the colors, layout and features you want, then refine the design as you go.

Try the prompt: Build me a professional personal portfolio website with a clean, modern design, a warm color palette and easy navigation. Include a homepage, an About Me section, a gallery of my work and a contact page. Make it mobile-friendly and easy to update. Use placeholder text and images that I can replace with my own content. Explain how to preview the website and publish it online when I'm ready.

Create a weekly dinner planner that generates a shopping list based on your selections. You could even add a feature that rotates your family's favorite meals.

Try the prompt: Build me a weekly meal-planning app that lets me plan dinners from Monday through Sunday and automatically generates a grocery shopping list based on my selections. Include a recipe library where I can save my family's favorite meals, customize serving sizes and rotate meals to avoid repetition. Organize the shopping list by grocery store department and let me check off items as I shop. Give it a clean, colorful, mobile-friendly design and save my meal plans locally. Explain how to open and use the finished app.

Ask Claude to develop a tool that identifies duplicate files, categorizes downloads or renames photos. Start with copies of your files and ask Claude to preview its proposed changes.

Try this prompt: Build me a file organization tool that identifies duplicate files, sorts downloads into folders by file type and renames photos by date. Start with a test folder containing copies of my files. Preview all proposed changes and ask for my approval before moving, renaming or deleting anything.

From personalized trivia games to interactive math quizzes for your kids, Claude Code can help you create something entertaining without downloading a game development platform.Try this prompt: Build me an interactive trivia game that runs in my web browser. Include customizable categories such as animals, science, movies and math, with three difficulty levels suitable for kids and adults. Give players multiple-choice questions, immediate feedback, a running score and fun animations for correct answers. Include a multiplayer mode so family members can compete against each other. Make the design colorful, mobile-friendly and easy to navigate. Let me add my own trivia questions and explain how to open and play the finished game.

Start with Plan Mode. Claude Code can outline its approach before modifying your project. This gives you an opportunity to review what it's proposing and make adjustments before it starts building.

Be careful with permissions. Claude Code can modify files and execute commands. I recommend using manual approval settings when you're getting started. Never authorize an action you don't understand, and keep backups of important files.

Ask Claude to test its work. Once your project is finished, ask Claude to check for errors, test every button and make sure everything functions as expected. AI-generated software can contain bugs, even when it looks polished.

What makes Claude Code a lot of fun is that you can simply explain what you want and it will create it. Even if you've never coded at all or have no idea what writing code even looks like, you can build your own software. Just start slow and think about a small frustration in your everyday life that an app or website might be able to fix. You might be surprised by what you can build with a few well-written prompts.

#3300. Apple among the companies facing pressure from US senators over ‘nudify’ apps [U: Apple, TTP respond]

The Guardian reports that three US senators have sent letters to the CEOs of Apple, Google, and Meta, demanding answers about their failure to prevent access to AI-powered ‘nudify’ apps. Here are the details.

Last month, Apple updated its App Store rules in an attempt to crack down on apps that enable users to generate nonconsensual nude images.

According to the updated rules, apps that allow users to create AI-generated content must include safeguards against abuse, including tools to filter objectionable material, report offensive content, and block abusive users.

Apple also warns that apps used primarily for pornographic content or the objectification of real people may be removed from the App Store without notice.

While definitely well-intended, Apple’s changes came amid growing reports of AI-powered nudify apps, which easily allow users to generate nonconsensual intimate images.

Two months before these changes, Apple removed an app that allowed users to create pornographic deepfakes of real people after WIRED reached out for comment, which in turn came one month after San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu demanded that Apple and Google remove several nudify apps from their app stores.

Apple also removed several apps following investigations by the Tech Transparency Project (TTP), which published reports in January and April revealing that such apps were widely available on the App Store, sometimes even appearing in sponsored search results.

Throughout these investigations, Apple has maintained that nudify apps have always been prohibited under its App Review Guidelines, and that it proactively rejects and removes apps that violate its policies, including those flagged through user reports.

Apple, of course, is not alone in this challenge, with Google facing similar criticism over their availability on the Play Store, and Meta coming under scrutiny for allowing developers to advertise these apps on Facebook and Instagram, as highlighted in the WIRED report mentioned above.

Which brings us to today’s report from The Guardian.

According to The Guardian’s exclusive report, “three Senate Democrats sent letters to tech CEOs saying safeguards against nudification apps are insufficient on their platforms.”

A trio of US Senators say Apple and Google are failing to effectively detect and remove apps that can be used to generate nonconsensual nude or pornographic imagery. They also say Meta is continuing to profit off of ads for these so-called nudification apps that “victimize women and girls worldwide”.

The senators, namely Ron Wyden of Oregon, Ed Markey of Massachusetts, and Ben Luján of New Mexico, claim that in addition to failing to remove these apps, the companies may actually be profiting from their distribution and promotion.

Commenting on the letter, both Google and Meta said they prohibit such apps or their promotion and work to detect and remove violations from their platforms, broadly echoing what Apple has repeatedly stated when reached for comment in the past over these same issues.

However, Wyden’s office argues that simply reaffirming, or in Apple’s case, updating these policies, means little if the companies continue to struggle to enforce them.

Keith Chu, the chief communications adviser and deputy policy director to Wyden, said that clarifying policies is not the same thing as enforcing them. Despite the companies reaffirming the prohibition of these apps, they continue to proliferate across Apple and Google app stores or be promoted in ads on Meta platforms, he added.

In its latest investigation, published just last month, TTP found 135 apps capable of generating nude or pornographic imagery on the App Store and the Play Store, using accounts registered to 13-year-old boys.

Additionally, researchers found that even accounts configured with parental controls were able to download these apps without requiring parental approval.

Despite Apple and Google removing the apps identified in the investigation, The Guardian noted that these apps continued to work on devices where they had already been installed.

Now, Senator Wyden warns that Congress may need to step in if the companies fail to do a better job of cracking down on these apps.

To read The Guardian’s full report, follow this link.

Update, 8:40 p.m. ET: In a statement to 9to5Mac, Apple said:

“We designed the App Store to be a safe and trusted place for users. A number of the apps in the TTP report are mainstream photo and video editing tools with legitimate, widely used functionality, and do not have nudification or deepfake capabilities. We prohibit nudify apps on the App Store, and remove developers who add capabilities like it after the App Review process — a malicious tactic known as bait-and-switch. We previously removed 28 of the apps referenced in this report before it was shared with us and have taken action on the remaining apps found to violate our rules. The report also relies on testing from older software that does not reflect current Apple safety features, including expanded protections for teens and parental controls in Screen Time that give families the ability to block kids and teens from downloading apps rated above their age.”

Expanding on the safety features mentioned in its statement, Apple noted that teens aged 13 through 17 now have certain protections enabled by default, including web content filters, even if their parents haven’t configured any restrictions, and pointed to ⁠this support article for more information.

The company added that children under 13 are required to use Child Accounts, and that the report relied on its previous 17+ age rating system, which was replaced last year with a more granular system that includes 13+, 16+, and 18+ ratings.

Just curious. Why doesn't someone from Apple try out the app before approving it, rather than approving it and waiting until people complain? I know there are many thousands of apps on the App store. But given that Apple makes money off most of these apps, it could surely afford to hire a staff charged with reviewing submitted apps to ensure compliance with the App store's guidelines and requirements before making them available in the App store. What am I missing here?

Apple also noted that in its report, TTP counted apps depicting people in swimwear or lingerie, which the company said does not constitute nudification or, in itself, violate its guidelines.

As for parental controls, Apple explained that, although apps that exceed a child’s configured age restrictions won’t appear in curated App Store sections, they can still be found through search, allowing children to request permission to download them through Ask to Buy. Without parental approval, the download remains blocked.

Apple added that Ask to Buy is supposed to require parental approval even for purchases made using gift card balances, including subscriptions. The company said that if a purchase didn’t trigger an approval request, that would be unexpected behavior, and that it is investigating further.

Update, November 19, 4:00 p.m. ET: In response to Apple’s statement, TTP director Katie Paul reached out to 9to5Mac with the following comment:

Apple’s statement on nudify apps sidesteps important issues and leaves out key context. The company says it prohibits nudify apps but doesn’t address how its age rating system for apps contributes to the problem. TTP has shown how Apple relies on information provided by app developers to set age ratings—a self-reporting system that allows many nudify and pornographic apps to be misleadingly labeled a suitable for minors. Apple also continues to talk about removing nudify apps from the App Store, without mentioning that apps that are “removed” continue to be fully functional on people’s phones.

There are many questions about Apple’s policy on nudify apps that the statement fails to address. Apple has adopted a limited definition of “nudify.” The company defines nudify apps as capable of showing someone naked, not stripping them down to a bikini or lingerie. But the company also says it bans “creepy” and “nonconsensual intimate imagery.” What if an app is used to depict a woman in a bikini without her consent? We have asked Apple to clarify that and have not heard back.

As for Apple’s comment that TTP relied on “older software,” that may refer to the fact that Apple rolled out new child safety features in the fall. Our research was conducted in summer 2026. But many of Apple’s new features pertain to parent-supervised accounts on Apple, which have to be set up by a parent. Apple relies entirely on parents to go out of their way to locate and enable these settings. This raises obvious questions about how many people actually do this.
